# Carry-over backlog

Items this repo owes itself. An entry lives here when it is real, measured, and **not the
subject of any live plan** — the state that previously had no home, so it survived only by
being written into a plan about something else and vanished when that plan was discharged.

**This is the DISTRIBUTION's backlog, and it is not a push-candidate ledger.** A consumer's
`_bmad-output/ai-dlc-update/push-candidate-ledger.md` tracks what that consumer wants pushed
UPSTREAM to ai-dlc, and its receipts resolve against a pull's `theirs` ref with the verbs
`theirs_has` / `theirs_lacks`. This file tracks what ai-dlc owes ITSELF, its receipts resolve
against this working tree, and its verbs are `sh` / `has` / `lacks`. The two grammars are
mutually unreadable by each other's engine on purpose. Entry ids are `BL-`, never `PC-`.

**Read by** `scripts/backlog-reverify.sh`, which executes each entry's `verify:` receipt and
emits a status. **Rotated by** `scripts/backlog-rotate.sh`, which moves closed entries to
`docs/backlog.archive.md` — it moves, it never deletes. Neither ships; both are
distribution-only, as `core/fixtures/plan-shape/.dist-only` already is.

## Receipts

```
verify: sh <one-liner>              exit 0 = the fix is present -> CLOSE-CANDIDATE
                                    exit 9 = the receipt cannot measure its subject -> NEEDS-REVIEW
                                    any other non-zero = still reproduces -> STILL-LIVE
verify: has   <repo-rel-path> "<substr>"    close when the file CONTAINS the substring
verify: lacks <repo-rel-path> "<substr>"    close when the file LACKS it
verify: manual                      no mechanical predicate by design -> HAND-REVIEW
```

**Prefer `sh`.** The tree is right here and executable, which the consumer's ledger cannot
assume of the ref it greps. A receipt runs from the repo root with stdin closed, so it names
any input it reads as a file. A behavioural predicate asserts the defect itself and cannot be
anchored on prose the author invented to describe a wanted fix.

**An `sh` receipt that reads a tracked file asserts its anchor first.** Before it tests the defect,
it asserts on that same path something that exits 9 if absent: `grep -q '<identifier>' <path> ||
exit 9`, or the brace-group, `if !` or non-empty-extract forms of the same guard. This covers
`grep`, `awk`, `sed`, `cat`, `! grep`, a working-tree `git grep` and `git show HEAD:<path>`. A rename
inside the file then reads as exit 9 (NEEDS-REVIEW) instead of as a quiet exit 1. `[ -f <path> ]`
alone is not an anchor. The anchor pattern carries a real identifier of 4 or more characters, does
not match line 1 or a shebang, and the guard exits exactly 9. The anchor must survive the fix,
because R8 wants a closed receipt to exit exactly 0, and an anchor the fix removes fails the close
permanently. An irrelevant but real identifier is left to review. This is enforced by R10 of
`scripts/validate-backlog-receipts.sh` (ceiling 0, `--max-unanchored`). Only history reads at a
non-HEAD revision are exempt.

**THIS FILE'S `sh` POLARITY IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE CONSUMER LEDGER'S, AND THE TWO ARE WRITTEN
IN THE SAME SESSIONS.** Here, `scripts/backlog-reverify.sh:335-336` reads **exit 0 as "the fix
is present"** and non-zero as "still reproduces". In a consumer's push-candidate ledger,
`core/skills/ai-dlc-update/reconcile/ledger-reverify.sh:2929` reads it the other way — **exit 0
means the entry STILL REPRODUCES**, and non-zero proposes CLOSE-CANDIDATE. Carrying this file's
rule into a consumer receipt writes a predicate that proposes closing a LIVE defect, which is
the one direction that loses data permanently. Check which file your receipt lands in before
you fix its polarity, and read the emitter rather than either header.

**In a consumer receipt, guard the unresolvable subject too.** A RENAMED subject also exits
non-zero there, so a relocation reads as an absorption that never happened; `[ -n "$s" ] ||
exit 127` makes it NEEDS-REVIEW instead. This file's engine needs no such guard, because its
non-zero direction is the one that keeps the entry open.

**When you must use `has`/`lacks`, anchor on a token the fix CANNOT BE WRITTEN WITHOUT** — a
flag, a path, a function name — never a phrase describing the fix. The consumer's engine
detects that error by reading a third ref; this one has no third ref to read, so the rule is
enforced by the author and by review, not by the tool. `core/fixtures/ledger-reverify-unfalsifiable/README.md`
is the measurement: 13 entries on the reference consumer carried predicates that could never
have gone green, and would have reported "still open" forever.

**A closed entry is annotated in place and left for rotation**, in the form
`**LANDED (v<version>, verified <sha>).**` — the annotation FORM is what the rotator keys on,
never the word anywhere in prose, because an entry that merely discusses landing something is
not a closed entry.

## BL-538 — the lead takes a full turn for every agent notification while an armed join already covers it

**PARTIAL (v0.794.0, verified 8aab009d) — the prose half shipped; the hook and the measurement are OPEN.** rule-28 states the lead's response to a notification a live beat covers (no status line, no re-check) and the two that are not covered. Correction at v0.796.0: 0.794.0 said "arming the beat ships with the wait release"; that release's rule-28 paragraph arms the serial remediator's join with `--complete-repair`, which is BL-541's subject, and carries nothing for this entry. Still owed: the optional hook that injects the response when the notified agent's deliverable is inside a live beat's path set, and the per-wake count re-measured on the next consumer sprint.

**DEFECT (efficiency).** In graph s319 lead session `62eadbbe-59c3-436d-bf7c-931ebc09ecba`, measured at 22:47Z: 109 `<task-notification>` wakes, of which 61 ended with no tool call and only a restatement that the join was still armed ("X delivered … the join beat is still armed, so I'm waiting"). Each such turn re-reads the lead's whole context. That context ran 250–320K tokens (the sensor fired yellow at 252,985 and the snapshot records red readings of 317,305 and 324,185), and by 21:37Z the session had already spent 61 M tokens of lead cache read over 272 API calls. The waits it restates are `wait-for-deliverable.sh --complete` beats over the whole round, which return on their own. Core says what a notification MEANS for the cap-release rule (`rule-28.md:195`) but nowhere what the lead should DO with one that arrives while a beat covers that agent's deliverable. The analysis this backlog is filed from ranks lead waiting among the largest costs (`docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s317-s318.md`, headline and "Relation to the v0.380.0 investigation").

Owed: a stated lead response to a notification for an agent whose deliverable an armed beat covers: no per-agent status line, no re-check, end the turn. Optionally, a hook that injects that instruction when the notified agent's deliverable is inside `.beat-inflight`'s path set. Measure it by re-running the per-wake count on the next consumer sprint.

**Second reading (f7 measured; transcript-only, not re-derived here).** In graph's s319 lead session `c61a91eb`, 20 of 29 task-notification wakes ended with no tool call. Method, f7's heuristic: a wake counts as ending with no tool call when no `tool_use` block appears before the next user line. This is NOT the same series as the filing's 61 of 109, which is a different session (`62eadbbe`), a different count of wakes, and was classed by whether the turn only restated that the join was armed; the two ratios (20/29 and 61/109) are two readings and are not a trend. Both say most wakes under an armed beat end without acting.

**Sharper reading (f7 measured; transcript-only, not re-derived here).** In graph's s319 lead session `c61a91eb`, on 0.828.0, one 25-agent SM seat ran under a single armed join (task `brrt6rqjh`). Between 14:40:41Z and 14:48:20Z (transcript lines 2702-2838) the lead took 14 consecutive wakes whose entire output was "Covered by the armed join; no action." Each was a full turn over a context of about 318k tokens or more, past the RED threshold. By f7's heuristic, the same method as the paragraph above, idle wakes went from 20 of 37 to 37 of 54: 17 in about 8 minutes on one round. The round plans 4 seats of about 25 agents each, so about 70 such turns are expected per round; that figure is f7's projection, not a count. Reading: the 0.794.0 prose half shortened each turn's output but cannot remove the turns; only the hook half can.

**Evidence (HANDOFF, 0.876.0).** The precondition for the hook half is in: the architect, analyst and ux deliverables now carry every item their return carried (`## Architect handoff`, `## Gaps`, `## Design decisions`), and SubagentStop keeps each final message in `_bmad-output/.subagent-final/<agent_id>.txt`. No hook is installed and this entry stays open.

**Evidence (HOOKWAKE).** The hook half ships as a UserPromptSubmit hook, `core/hooks/ai-dlc-hookwake.sh`, that BLOCKS a subagent hand-back while that agent's wait beat is outstanding. It joins on the `.wait-beats/.beat-argv-<pid>` record `core/scripts/wait-for-deliverable.sh` writes at arm time, with the start time read through the shared `core/scripts/wfd-start-of.sh`, and `core/fixtures/hookwake` drives it in both layouts. That is a different shape from the "hook that injects that instruction" this entry names: it refuses the wake rather than telling the lead how to answer it. The measurement half, a re-taken wake count on a consumer lead session, is still OPEN, so the entry stays PARTIAL.

**Progress (batch 240).** The flip half needs a redesign before it returns to the operator: `wait-for-deliverable.sh` records dispatch-to-path pairs at arm time, J4 becomes per-agent, C5 gets a guaranteed carrier, and the design is checked against a captured real UserPromptSubmit payload.

**Progress (batch b248; measured by the batch b248 lead, ai-dlc-f8; the entry stays PARTIAL).** The round-dispatcher design is a small subagent that owns each wide round and returns to the lead once; the operator chose to probe it before building. Probe 1 (Claude Code 2.1.316): a subagent spawned 6 background agents, all 6 completion notifications reached that subagent and 0 reached the parent session, so notifications route to the spawning subagent. Probe 2 (headless `claude -p`, haiku): with CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS=2, the child's dispatcher took slot 1 and its first nested spawn took slot 2, and the 2nd and 3rd nested spawns were REFUSED, not queued, with `Concurrent subagent limit reached. You can run 2 subagents at once. Do not retry. ...`; the control at cap 10 accepted all 4 spawns. So the cap counts every live subagent at any nesting depth, and the top-level session takes no slot. Consequence for the design: a dispatcher holds one slot for its whole round, so it reduces the lead's wakes but not its concurrency; it must size its waves to the cap minus every other live subagent, and an over-cap spawn fails hard, so its "Do not retry" text must be handled as a refusal, not as a failed agent. The raw evidence is two stream-json scratch files, `cap2.jsonl` and `cap10.jsonl`, which are not committed, so these figures cannot be re-derived from the tree.

**Progress (batch b249, c5, 0.1000.0; the entry stays PARTIAL until its outcome line).** Re-measure on s321, counted by f7's heuristic (a wake counts as ending with no tool call when no `tool_use` block appears before the next user line) over four graph lead transcripts, `2c84f6b7`, `59a855bd`, `d9d2b30c` and `38d6a63b`, all entrypoint `cli` on Claude Code 2.1.312 to 2.1.317: 270 task-notification wakes, of which 150 were idle, 56%. The control is that the same counter, run on the s319 `c61a91eb` window, reproduces 37 idle of 54 exactly. Split by kind with the contract adversary's classifier, 197 wakes were agent exits and 153 of them idle, while 81 were background-command completions and only 2 of them idle, so the idle turns are almost entirely agent-exit notifications. Two 28-agent rounds took 20 and 16 idle wakes in their windows; those windows run to the next round and therefore over-count. Correction to the batch-b248 paragraph's probe 1: on Claude Code 2.1.317 a child's completion notification reaches its spawner only while the spawner is running. A spawner that ends its turn with live background children sends its parent an interim notification ("... is waiting on its own background work", status `completed`) and is re-woken once per child, while a spawner held inside a single foreground call until every child finished woke its parent exactly once. Measured interactively with 3 children, the background-beat variant woke the top session 2 times and the foreground variant once, and a headless run agrees. Nested agents' meta files land flat in the top session's `subagents/` directory with `parentAgentId` and `spawnDepth: 2`, and share the top session's `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`; a child given a `name` becomes an in-process teammate at `spawnDepth` 1. This release ships the round-dispatcher: Rule 28 "Split dispatch", the 28(a) carve-out, the `_dispatch-protocol.md` "Round-dispatcher brief" section, the handoff guard counting a dispatcher's members, and the `foreground-budget-deny` fixture pins that allow (a subagent's foreground `AI_DLC_WAIT_BEAT_SECS=540 ... wait-for-deliverable.sh` call at `timeout: 600000` is allowed, a poll-shaped twin is denied, the same call from the lead is denied). Its scope is the adversarial-pass, elicitation and party-seat rounds; review/QA, repair, gate-adjudicator and dev rounds stay lead-dispatched. The raw probe transcripts are scratch and uncommitted, so the probe figures above cannot be re-derived from the tree. Under the batch-147 ruling no model replay closes a prompt fix; the close is the structural trace plus the pin fixture named by the entry's `verify:` line, and the per-wake count on the next consumer sprint is the outcome measurement, recorded when taken and not a close condition. The entry is tagged `**DEFECT (efficiency).**`, so under BL-817 it closes only with that `Outcome measured:` line, taken on the first graph sprint that runs this release; until then it stays PARTIAL. NOTE: the dispatcher runs on the lead's model, holding member brief paths and spending its round inside foreground waits; a team-roles binding (role file, aiDlcRoles row, definition) is the remedy if its cost shows up.

**Progress (batch b249, c5, party rounds; operator ruling 2026-11-03 "Include in c5 (Recommended)").** Sharded party rounds are now per-seat role-bound `Agent` spawns that a round-dispatcher may run, while an unsharded round stays on the `/bmad-party-mode` Skill, and Rule 20 gains shape (v). The record of a sharded seat is the dispatch guard's spawn-ledger row, written by the hook, plus the seat's `--mark` line; seats write no provenance block, Check 17 runs no arm on a seat file, and a block stamped on afterwards is a forged record. `join-remediator-shards.sh` refuses a sharded seat file that has no role-bound row of that sprint, role and shard. It judges only when the installed `_gate-procedures.md` carries the new record sentence and otherwise prints `SEAT-ROWS: SKIP`, because the engine reaches a consumer at pull step 3 and the rulebook only at the reconcile merge. Ground truth from graph, measured read only: s321's 56 seat files carry 0 party provenance blocks, against 164 in s318 and 130 in s320, and all 56 seat spawns have role-bound, contract-cited ledger rows; the s321 architecture party round had 28 seats. s318's carry-over gate failed Check 17 on 40 blockless seat files, after which a remediator stamped 40 blocks with `tool_use_id: NOT_ACCESSIBLE`. Measured with the shipping function on copies, the false-positive set with the boundary in place is 0 refused in s318, s320 and s321, because graph's installed rulebook lacks the sentence. With the boundary forced on, it is 0 in s321 (56 files), 87 of 295 in s318 and 152 of 280 in s320; those are pre-ruling rounds (the Skill path, or per-group `cross/<K> g1/<G>` shards) that the boundary exists to skip. NOTE: A party round whose findings need no repair is never joined, so its seats are never checked. NOTE: Spawn-ledger rows carry no step, so a seat also matches rows from another round of the same sprint. K is therefore taken as the shard count common to every row-bearing seat of the round, the smallest when several are shared. A round sharing none is refused, naming its Ks. The literal reading, refuse when rows disagree on K, was rejected because it refused both of graph's s321 party rounds, whose union of row Ks is {6, 13}. A row from another round with the same role, ordinal and K can still cover a hand-written seat. NOTE: A round is judged only if its latest matched spawn-ledger row (or, without one, its seat files' newest add commits) is at or after the oldest commit whose `git log -S` adds the seat-row sentence to the installed `_gate-procedures.md`. An earlier round prints `SEAT-ROWS: SKIP legacy-round <step>`, and an unreadable date skips with its reason. A seat-ledger row older than the install dates its round but never covers a seat or names a K. A round with no row at or after the install is dated by its seat files when every seat file is committed and clean, each by its newest add commit, so a seat deleted and re-added after the install is judged: it is legacy only if all of them predate the install, and otherwise it is judged. The seat list is the scan's own sharded-seat parse, so an unsharded `<step>-<role>.md` or another step's seat beside the round does not enter it. A round with any uncommitted seat, or any seat that is modified, staged or untracked in one `git status --porcelain` over its seats, prints `SEAT-ROWS: SKIP round-undatable <step> <n> seats` and is judged once its seats are committed. A round is therefore judged whenever any of its matched rows is at or after the install, which closes the case where a new round in the same sprint matches an older round's rows. Measured on copies of graph's s318 records with a simulated install commit dated after 2026-10-14T16:04:44Z, which is when graph commit 28a15fce4 first added all 295 s318 seat files: `requirements-party-repair` (36 seat refusals at e49446c61) and `stories-party-repair-p1-d3` (19) skip as legacy rounds with rc 0 there. Graph itself has no install commit today, so on graph the join prints the rulebook-sentence `SEAT-ROWS: SKIP` line instead. s321 architecture joins its 28 seats with 0 refusals. NOTE: `sprint-review.md` says its party round is always sharded and has no line for a one-story or SERIAL map, unlike `carry-over-evaluation.md`. NOTE: The resident Rule 20 stub in `SKILL.md` names the sub-skills' `mode: subagent` provenance and does not mention shape (v). The full Rule 20 text it loads does. NOTE: `receipt-bl538.sh` creates a `mktemp -d` and does not remove it. (`receipt-bl538.sh` was deleted in 0.1019.0; the `verify:` line now runs the fixture.) NOTE: A round in which every seat bypassed the dispatch guard and every seat file is still uncommitted at join time is skipped as undatable, not refused. NOTE: A re-run that overwrites committed pre-install seat files and then COMMITS the overwrite, with no post-install row, still reads `legacy-round`, because the seats are dated by their add commits and a committed modification is not an add.

**Progress (batch b249, c5, seat file on the ledger row; lead ruling).** This closes a defect in the seat-row join described above. Spawn-ledger rows carry no step, so re-joining an earlier step of a sprint that straddles the install matched a later step's post-install rows, judged the earlier round and refused its seats. It was measured on copies of graph's s321 ledger with the install dated 2026-11-01: `requirements-party-repair` gave rc 2 with 14 seat refusals, where it had read legacy before the per-round change. The dispatch guard now writes `mark_file` onto each spawn-ledger row: the last `party-mode/s<N>/<basename>` tail in the brief's single `--mark` invocation, stopping at a blank or a quote, so a blank in the consumer's root cannot cut it, or the path as written when it carries no such tail. It is written only when exactly one `--mark` invocation is present, and it is not proof that the file exists. The seat-row join matches a row carrying it ONLY to the seat file whose path ends in that `party-mode/s<N>/<basename>` tail. That row never enters step, ordinal or K inference, and it covers its seat only when its role matches, it is role-bound, and it is stamped at or after the install. A pre-install field-row dates its seat and covers nothing. One pair of surrounding quotes is stripped. A `mark_file` with no usable tail names no seat file and is read as a field-less row, and it infers only for seats that no usable-tail row names. Rows from an older guard keep the field-less inference. Measured read only on graph's lead transcripts, across 140 party-seat spawns (s321 28+28, s320 70, s319 14): the brief's `--mark` path, reduced to its `party-mode/s<N>/<basename>` tail, equals the file the seat wrote in 140 of 140, and the negative control (the next seat's writes) is 0 of 140. 112 of the 140 paths are absolute, which is why the match is by tail and never by root. The guard was driven base against tip over 5309 real graph Agent payloads: decisions are identical on 5309 of 5309, rows are identical on 5288 of 5288 once `mark_file` is set aside, `mark` is kept on all 1344 rows that carried it, and no fork is added. On graph's real ledger, which has 0 `mark_file` rows, all 43 field-less join runs read identically before and after. With the architecture rows given `mark_file`, the DEFECT-1 world reads `SKIP legacy-round requirements`, rc 0. 0 of 1969 real `--mark` briefs quote their path, and 182 of 182 real seat-tail rows carry the seat's own role. NOTE: a field-row is matched on its seat basename alone, so a post-install field-row from an earlier run of the same step covers the re-run's same-named seat at any K, and a round whose seats are all field seats has no K to disagree on. Owed, under the step-value ruling in `.claude/rules/operator-rulings.md` ("A step with no measured value goes") applied to fixtures — a fixture or mutant shard stays only on evidence, a named defect class it catches that no other unit catches; without that the batch retires or merges it, and it is not put to the operator as a choice:
1. Rank by cost first: the mutant batteries, then the non-mutant poles.
2. For each sharded battery, measure whether its mutants kill anything the base fixture's arms do not; shards of one battery that kill the same set are redundant.

**PARTIAL (v0.1164.0) — the outside-`FIXTURE_POOL` row is narrowed, the dead guard is deleted, and the Owed list is re-derived; the pole value judgment and the rows still listed under Owed stay open.**
- Outside-`FIXTURE_POOL`, part B. The I66 unit in `scripts/validate-enforcement-map.sh` derives each pre-push hook's pool names (column-0 `name()` definitions, `NAME=` assignments and `rec_home NAME` lines between the sentinels) and fails on any non-comment line outside the pool that defines one of those functions or assigns one of those globals. A `local` declaration does not count. A line ending `# pool-shadow: subshell` is exempt only inside an open `( … )` block (opened by a line matching `^[ \t]*\( `, closed on the line where the count of `(` minus `)` since the opener returns to 0), and only in the distribution hook. A marked line outside any block fails I66, and so does any `# pool-shadow:` line in `core/git-hooks/pre-push`. A block still open at the end of either hook fails I66 too, naming the hook and the opener line. The count includes parens inside strings, so an unbalanced `(` in a string fails closed this way, and an unbalanced `)` fails loud (BL-1161, claim 3). The false-positive set before the marker was measured with the shipping awk: `.githooks/pre-push:275-276` (the `ps_select` key-pass subshell, which reassigns `KEYS_DIR`, `FXROOT`, `READSET_MAP`, `READSET_LOCAL` and `VERIFIED_RECORD` and redefines `readset_drop_excluded`), and none in `core/git-hooks/pre-push`. Those two lines carry the marker. An empty name set fails closed.
- Outside-`FIXTURE_POOL`, part A. The REFUSED → exit 2 tail of each hook now sits between `# FIXTURE_EXIT_BEGIN` and `# FIXTURE_EXIT_END`. I66 holds that span sound in both hooks (exactly one BEGIN and one END, in order, with code between them) and holds the two spans identical once comments and blanks are stripped. The BLOCKED block stays outside the span. `core/fixtures/consumer-suite-pool/run.sh:809-818` asserts exit 2 for a lone refusal on the consumer hook, with its exit-1 twin at `:803-806`. I66 binds the distribution hook's tail to be identical to it. No fixture asserts the `pre-push: REFUSED.` banner line: `grep -c` gives 0 in that fixture, against 2 for `exits 2`. That gap is BL-1161.

## BL-806 — a lead can write an estimated, future-dated time into `pipeline-snapshot.md`, and a resuming session reads it as fact

**DEFECT.** Filed at the batch-242 close from the graph watch (ai-dlc-fa, poll 30, 03:42 EDT 2026-10-26). At 07:39:12Z graph's s320 lead ran a `sed` that wrote `| 18/19 delivered at 07:50Z (still out: cross-1 only …` into `_bmad-output/pipeline-snapshot.md`. That stamp is 11 minutes after the moment it was written. The row's previous value read `16/19 delivered at 07:35Z`, so the time was estimated, not taken from `date`. `core/skills/ai-dlc/SKILL.md:52` makes a resuming session read that file in full before any pipeline action, so a wrong time there becomes a resuming lead's premise. No outcome was affected this time.

Owed: a check, not an instruction, because the instruction to take times from `date` exists in this repo's own rules and was not followed. Either the snapshot writer stamps times itself, or a hook or validator refuses a snapshot time later than the write's own clock. Measure the false-positive set first: a deliberately future time (a stated deadline) must be spelled differently from a delivery stamp.

**Progress (batch 243; the entry stays PARTIAL, `verify: manual` unchanged, no LANDED line).** Part (a) shipped; part (b) is owed.

**(a) shipped.** Deny B in `core/hooks/ai-dlc-foreground-budget.sh` (`elif ... then "DENY B"` at `:248`, header `# DENY B, A SHELL WRITE OF THE SNAPSHOT` at `:81-122`) refuses a Bash call that names `pipeline-snapshot.md` (as a path ending there; `pipeline-snapshot-history.md` appends stay allowed) and carries a write shape: `sed`/`perl` with `-i`/`--in-place`, a `>`/`>>` redirect onto it, `tee [-a]`, `cp|mv|install|ln` with it as the last operand, `git checkout|restore` of it, or an interpreter write (`open(…,'w'|'a'|'x'|'+')`, `.write_text(`, `.write_bytes(`, `writeFileSync`) on the literal path or on a variable bound to it earlier in the command. Reads stay allowed (`cat`, `grep`, `sed -n`, `<`, `python3 open(p)`, `cp` from it, `git add/commit/show/diff`). It is an early branch decided before every scope gate and fail-open, so no timeout, `agent_id` or missing detector exempts it. The remedy is the Edit or Write tool, so `ai-dlc-derivation-capture.sh` judges the written stamps; that hook's own header (`core/hooks/ai-dlc-derivation-capture.sh:134`, "reaches no PostToolUse hook") says a Bash `sed -i` on the snapshot reaches no PostToolUse hook, which is how the motivating `07:50Z` row went unjudged.

Measurement 0a, driving the shipped hook over graph's transcripts: 4,617 Bash calls name the snapshot and 1,912 are denied (1,905 by Deny B and 7 by Deny A, which fires on the waiter shape in the same corpus; 1,873 distinct). Of the 1,905 Deny B records (1,866 distinct), an independent second reading tags 1,740 by write shape: interpreter open-w 1,630, `sed -i` 121, cp/mv 10, tee 7, `git restore` 3 and redirect 2. These are tag counts, and a record can carry more than one, so they sum to 1,773. The other 165 records (164 distinct) carry no tag from that reading. A quote-aware scan of each `sed -i` invocation's file operand resolves all 164 distinct records to the snapshot, so they are `sed -i` writes that the reading's regex did not tokenise. The false-positive set is empty by an independent second reading. The fail-closed alternative (deny any command naming the snapshot unless it starts with a whitelisted read verb) was measured on the same corpus and rejected: it denied 1,465 commands that are not writes. Over `core/` and `templates/` (`core/fixtures` excluded) there are 517 payloads and exactly 1 deny, the validator's own self-probe body at `core/scripts/validate-artifact-budget.sh:1951` (`} > "$LPROBE_D/state/pipeline-snapshot.md"`), which is script body and not a command an agent issues. No core script takes the snapshot path as an argument and writes it.

(a)'s receipt, QUOTED and not installed (the entry's receipt line stays manual): drive the shipped hook with `{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"sed -i '' 's/a/b/' _bmad-output/pipeline-snapshot.md"}}` and require a deny naming Edit; require `sed -n 1p _bmad-output/pipeline-snapshot.md` and a `>>` onto `pipeline-snapshot-history.md` to be allowed; the `sed -i.bak` spelling must also deny. It has not been scored here; the fixture arms of the hook change carry the scored form.

**(b) owed, and blocked on the CLOCK and two GRAMMAR gaps.** The clock: history carries only commit time (below). The grammar: a range end whose start carries no `Z` is missed, and a date-only stamp is skipped by the date rule, so its bare time is dated a day late (both in the census lower bound below). No arm ships until the re-filed evidence below exists. **Ship criterion: an arm ships only with a derived false-positive set that is EMPTY or ENUMERATED.** The N ≥ 300 exit condition below is the condition for RE-MEASURING, not a ship standard; a re-measurement that leaves an unenumerated false positive ships nothing. BL-912 does not subsume (b): `snapshot-update.sh` calling `--stamps-only` carries the same bare `HH:MMZ` gap.
- Census (batch 253, graph's committed history, file:// clone, read-only). Population: `git log --all --no-merges -- _bmad-output/pipeline-snapshot.md`, 1,190 commits; the HEAD-simplified history holds only 565, which the first b253 measurement took and was wrong. 11,859 distinct added lines, each deduped to its introducing commit. Rule: a bare `HH:MM(:SS)?Z` is dated from the nearest preceding dated stamp in its line (else from now's date), with previous-day rollover only and the `CLOCK CORRECTION` `to date -u:` token list exempt; it fires when more than 600 s ahead of now. Stamp-led Recent Activity (2,499 lines): 113 fires on 75 distinct lines with now = the parent commit's time (upper bound). Every other line (9,360): 78 fires on 63 distinct lines (upper). Of the 191 upper-bound fires, 116 carry a token that resolves at or before the line's own leading stamp. Under the commit's own clock 182 of the 191 stop firing (191 − 9). Lower bound, with now = the commit's own time: 9 fires on 9 distinct lines (2 stamp-led Recent Activity, 7 other), in 4 categories. 3 are range ends the grammar misses when the start carries no `Z` (`15:40-22:30Z`, `13:30→14:00Z`, `14:40→16:10Z`). 3 are lines with no dated stamp, whose bare time is dated from the commit clock. 1 is a date-only stamp (`- 2026-10-12 …`) that the date rule skips, so its `08:40Z` is dated a day late. 2 lead with a stamp that is itself ahead of the commit, which the existing FUTURE arm already fires on. The motivating `| 18/19 delivered at 07:50Z` row was never committed (`git log --all -S'delivered at 07:35Z'` = 0 against a positive control). Its text is a TABLE CELL, and five `snapshot-update.sh` ops write such text with rc 0: `--row-set <a> deliverable`, `--line-replace 'In-Flight Teammates'`, `--set in_flight_sub_step`, `--activity` with no leading stamp, and `--open-item`. Any future arm's population includes all five.

A 12 h previous-day rule removes 137 of them. The remainder is 184 `~` approximations, 35 range ends, 1 stray `T` and 72 other in 22 distinct texts, all false positives (times on another date, quoted past times); 0 true positives. The motivating write is a Bash `sed` at 2026-10-26T07:39:12Z in `d22c7889…jsonl`, with `07:50Z` 648 s ahead; it is invisible to the write-time hook, and Deny B now refuses it. Edit payloads: 163 token fires without a rollover rule, 133 with. After narrowing (`~`, range ends, CLOCK CORRECTION/NOTE lines, 12 h rollover, backticked) about 55 fire, about 51 true positives and about 4 false positives, BY HAND CLASSIFICATION, not a derived count. An FP class that cannot be enumerated remains: a quoted earlier time under 12 h old (`08:57:12Z` quoted at 00:38). Controls: `99:99Z` 0; the motivating row matches. Eight CLOCK CORRECTION rewrites by graph leads show the true-positive class is real.

Of measurement 2's 5,236 jsonl, 356 are reachable now (`find /Users/n8/.claude/projects/-Users-n8-git-graph -name '*.jsonl' | wc -l`), and the oldest record is 2026-11-09T00:00Z. `d22c7889*` is absent under `$HOME` and `/private/tmp` (`/usr/bin/find`; the control, a present file's 8-character prefix under `$HOME`, returns 4). Measurement 2's text above is now the only instance of its evidence, and its by-hand counts cannot be re-derived.
- Re-filed evidence requirement. Since BL-912 (0.1012.0) every snapshot write is a `snapshot-update.sh` Bash tool_use, and that record's own `timestamp` is a true write clock. Measured in batch 253 over the 356 reachable files (records with `"type":"assistant"`, Bash `tool_use` blocks whose `input.command` invokes `snapshot-update.sh` with a write op, keyed by tool_use `id`, joined to their `tool_result` by `tool_use_id`). **Op-detection rule: an invocation is a write when any write-op flag appears anywhere in the invocation, not only the first flag after `snapshot-update.sh`** (a leading `--snapshot <path>` puts the op second). Cutoff: tool_use `timestamp` ≤ 2026-11-10T12:41:59.999Z. Result: 273 write invocations, 2026-11-09T00:21Z to 2026-11-10T12:41Z; 252 returned without `is_error`, and 39 of those carry at least one bare `HH:MM(:SS)?Z` in the command text, an upper bound on writes adding one, since old-text and key arguments count too. A first-flag-only reading of the same population found 262, 242 and 37; it missed 11 writes and found none the any-flag reading lacks. Control: `99:99Z` matches 0. Sufficiency, in writes: zero fires in N bare-bearing writes bounds the FP rate below about 3/N at 95%, so excluding a 1% FP rate needs N ≥ 300 (the point where a 1% rate predicts 3 fires). Today 39 × 1% predicts 0.39 fires, below one, so a zero now refutes nothing. At the measured 39/252, 300 bare-bearing writes means 300 × 252 / 39 = 1,938.5, so ≥ 1,939 rc-0 `snapshot-update.sh` writes. The reachable transcripts span about 37 hours and held 252 such writes. `cleanupPeriodDays` is 365 in `~/.claude/settings.json`, and whether the window is rolling was not established. **Exit condition: re-measure when the post-BL-912 rc-0 `snapshot-update.sh` write population, ACCUMULATED across successive captures of graph's transcripts and deduped by tool_use `id`, holds ≥ 300 writes whose command text carries a bare token, counted by the strict grammar stated in the batch-256 Progress paragraph below; until then the check waits.** Meeting it starts a re-measurement; it does not ship an arm, which still needs the ship criterion above. The measurement then runs on that population with now = the tool_use `timestamp` and the census rule above, and counts four arms separately: stamp-led Recent Activity; the five table and key ops; the range-end-without-`Z` miss; and the `CLOCK CORRECTION` exemption.

**Progress (batch 256, M6; the entry stays PARTIAL, `verify: manual` unchanged, no LANDED line).** The exit condition is counted and not met, so the wait is confirmed and no arm is built.

The grammar, restated; it replaces the counting rule of the re-filed evidence bullet above:
- Write op: a whole-token flag from the case arms of `core/scripts/snapshot-update.sh` (`--snapshot)` at `:258` through `--init)` at `:291`) other than `--snapshot`. That is 19 flags: `--activity`, `--open-item`, `--row-add`, `--close-item`, `--row-delete`, `--open-item-file`, `--row-status`, `--row-set`, `--set`, `--key-delete`, `--set-block`, `--section-add`, `--section-move-to-history`, `--row-replace`, `--line-add`, `--line-replace`, `--line-delete`, `--move-to-history`, `--init`. Whole-token matters because `--open-item` is a prefix of `--open-item-file`, `--set` of `--set-block`, and `--activity` of `--activity-add`.
- Invocation: from `snapshot-update.sh` to the end of its command segment.
- Bare token: `(?<![0-9T:])\d\d:\d\d(:\d\d)?Z`, so the time inside a full ISO stamp does not count.
- Lower bound: graph's install of 0.1012.0, 2026-11-05T23:58:28Z, from graph's history.
- The deciding quantity is rc-0 writes carrying a bare token, against 300.

Reading, from the bl806 hand's corpus taken 2026-11-12T18:12:16Z: 6315 jsonl files under `~/.claude/projects/-Users-n8-git-graph`, newest write 2026-11-12T12:48:49Z. decides a step is the step-value rule (`docs/analysis/step-value-s317-s319.md`, "A step with no measured value
goes" in `.claude/rules/operator-rulings.md`): a step, round or fan-out width is kept on a named failure case and
on catches no other step makes that survive to the shipped artifact, and a rare high-consequence catch is judged
on consequence, not frequency. So each entry here closes on a measured graph sprint, read by
`docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s317-s320/scripts/`, that states what its own step's machine hours and tokens
per story did against s317 and s319. A cost that fell closes the entry. A cost that did not fall closes it only
with that rule's evidence for what the cost buys; without it, the cost is waste the entry still owes. The s317 and
s319 figures beside each entry are reference points, not pass bars: a fixed bar can be met by cutting a step that
catches real defects, which the rule forbids. An entry whose mechanism has shipped and whose sprint has not been
measured is PARTIAL, whatever its `verify:` line says. BL-817 makes this a mechanism.

## BL-809 — a re-review pass is spent on evidence and bookkeeping findings that a validator could settle, so a story is reviewed up to nine times

**DEFECT (efficiency).** Graph s319 ran 44 gate-1 re-review passes over 23 reviewed stories. s317 ran 13 over 21
and s318 ran 16 over 14. Story 3.1 ran 9 passes: p5, p8 and p9 carried 0 findings, and p4, p6 and p7's findings
are capture labels, `$` lines, stale citations and story-record wording.

  (167 matched an evidence or bookkeeping keyword set). That is a heading-keyword classification and a floor of
  unknown precision. The derived form is a finding under a part whose map row is entirely captures.

  passes silently on null), so the round itself is not the defect.

  measurement, and the rest still return as review findings.

Owed:
1. A NEEDS_REWORK whose every Critical and Important finding is evidence or bookkeeping re-checks through
   `validate-handoff-evidence.sh` and the one serial reviewer it names, not through a fresh fan-out.
2. A re-review whose delta, captures excluded (BL-808), touches no more than one code file dispatches one serial
   reviewer.
3. Extend the validator to the evidence classes s319's findings show it does not refuse: a capture labelling the
   wrong commit, a `$` line that cannot replay, and a stale per-AC citation.

Item 1 is the wall-clock lever and is not optional. A re-review pass is a serial wait (rework, freeze, review)
whatever its width, so a narrower pass removes dollars and a removed pass removes hours. BL-808 makes passes
narrower and removes none. Reference points: gate-1 re-review passes per reviewed story read 0.62 in s317 (13
over 21) and 1.91 in s319 (44 over 23); implementation plus gate-validation[implementation] machine hours per
story (`steps.csv` active plus agent wait, operator wait excluded) read 1.87 (s317: old clock, not reproducible) and 1.80 (s319: old clock; 1.34 h on the monotone clock, BL-1174 C5 reading, tree c4b7f370a). The measured sprint reports
both. A re-review pass is earned by a code finding the pass caught; a pass spent only on evidence or bookkeeping a
validator could settle is the waste this entry removes. The implementation spawn and dollar figure is reported
jointly with BL-808.

**Status (this release).** PARTIAL. Items 1 and 2 shipped, and item 3 shipped in part (its still-owed arms are below); `verify: manual` until the measured sprint.

Item 1, the record-only route. Each Critical/Important finding carries one `Class: CODE|TEST|EVIDENCE|BOOKKEEPING` line (owner `code-reviewer.md`; TEST is code-class; a finding admitting any code fix is CODE). `merge-review-shards.sh` refuses a value outside the set and accepts a missing one. `partition-review-diff.sh --route` routes a re-review to `validate-handoff-evidence.sh` plus one serial reviewer only when every prior Critical/Important finding is EVIDENCE or BOOKKEEPING and the delta from the prior `reviewed-sha:` to the frozen sha carries no code path. It sends the pass full on zero findings, a missing or unknown Class, any unrouted finding, an unresolvable or non-ancestor sha, and an empty or unreadable delta. The delta's code class (`partition-review-diff.sh`, THE CODE CLASS) drops a path under a scan root, a `.md`, a `.txt/.log/.out` outside any test directory, or a `.txt/.log/.out` that `--list-captures` names; any code-extension file is code wherever it sits and whether or not the story cites it. Measured on graph with the shipped predicate: 0/3/6 routed passes (s317/s318/s319). M7's 4 for s318 used a `test-results/` path-prefix partition. The shipped class counts `test-results/red_splat_copy.py`, which the s318 2-3 story cites, as code, so s318 2-3-p3 goes full (fail closed). Labels: blind re-label disagreement was s317 13/86 (5 cross E|B) and s318 5/75 (1 crosses). Without the delta guard, s317 routes 3 passes on M7's labels and 1 on the blind labels, and the s317 2-6 miss appears under one labeller only. The guard removes it under both, so the delta guard is the safety property and Class is the saving.

Guard cost, PRICE / VALUE. VALUE is a pass the guard sent full whose re-review raised at least one CODE or TEST finding; PRICE is every other such pass (clean, or evidence and bookkeeping findings only). The guard sent 11 passes full that the class oracle would have routed: PRICE 10, VALUE 1. VALUE is a full re-review pass that caught a CODE or TEST finding the record-only route would have missed; a pass whose only findings are EVIDENCE or BOOKKEEPING is PRICE, because the route would have settled those.
- s317, PRICE 2, VALUE 1. 1-2-p3 and 1-2-p4 are PRICE. 2-6-p4 is VALUE: it caught 2 code findings that the s317 2-6 rework had introduced by deleting an assertion.
- s318, PRICE 3, VALUE 0. 1-1-p3 is PRICE: its one Important finding (the mutation captures are gitignored and not in the commit) is EVIDENCE. 2-3-p2 is PRICE: its two Important findings (`ac4-hunks.txt` and `ac1-ac3-green.txt` record no command or head sha; the close signal claims a RED for a binding that has no capture) are both EVIDENCE. 2-3-p3 is PRICE: APPROVED with no Critical or Important finding (its one Suggestion is the red-splat driver's exit code).

A CODE or TEST finding carries a column-0 `Files: <repo-relative path>[, ...]` line under its `Class:` line (owner `code-reviewer.md`). `merge-review-shards.sh` THE FILES LINE refuses it on any other class, when two appear in one finding, on an empty list, on an entry that is not a bare repo-relative path, and, at the merge and `--check-shard`, on an entry that is neither tracked at the frozen sha nor changed in the range. Method, the survival arm. Each C/M repair block's `claim now asserted` line gives its spans. A span that is absent from the target before the round and present at the ship ref is text the repair wrote that reached the shipped artifact (NEW-SHIPPED). The ship refs are the stories gate 41484a513 and the sprint merge fb6f198e7 for s321, and the sprint merge 1da426ef9 for s319. The arm is a FLOOR, for three reasons. It does not read a claim line that has no span (NO-SPAN), or a block that names no story (NO-TARGET). Text presence is not correctness. Correction (span grammar, BL-1132). `claim_spans()` had two pairing defects of its own. It blanked code spans before pairing double quotes, so a quoted story sentence that carried a code span could not match. And it paired a double-backtick span (`` `x` ``) as fragments. It now pairs code spans the way CommonMark does and double quotes over a position-preserving mask, and takes `bt_min`/`dq_min`. `adversarial_yield.py` calls it at 12+, and `arch_yield.py`'s overlap proxy calls it too, with byte-identical output.

## BL-508 — a repair pass writes the defects the next adversary pass finds

**DEFECT (efficiency).** Closed in 0.786.0 on a tree receipt, reopened by BL-817. Its decision rule is the step-value ruling, "A step with no measured value goes" (`.claude/rules/operator-rulings.md`).

**DEFECT. [efficiency rank 2] about $105 across both sprints.** In every planning series read
(carry-over, requirements, architecture) in both sprints, each MAJOR on pass 2 or 3 sat in text the
previous repair wrote or half-fixed: 19 traced, 16 read in full, one true re-find. In stories the
adversary labelled repair-introduced majors s317 p1 0/11, p2 2/9, p3 2/4 and s318 p1 16/30, p2 8/19,
p3 1/2. Typical forms: one copy fixed and its sibling left, line cites shifted, a false count written
by the repair. Costed as planning third passes that ran only because every pass-2 MAJOR was repair-made
($39 s318 + $2 s317), plus the stories repair-introduced share of later-pass adversary and
remediator spend (4/13 × $97 ≈ $30 s317, 9/21 × $80 ≈ $34 s318). The remediator's drop from
high to medium effort at the s317/s318 boundary coincides with the rise; that is confounded and is
graph's setting, not core's. Subsumes the earlier "adversary series length" finding.

Efficacy, re-read for the fix: about 10 of about 33 sampled repair-introduced MAJORs are a sibling
left unfixed or a moved cite; the rest are underived claims the existing evidence contract already
forbids. The fix reaches that third, so the $105 is not what it recovers. The fix: every `repaired`
entry with a real edit carries `- siblings:`. A files-mode shard writes a fence grepping the
replaced text over ONLY its own files (a concurrent shard fixing a copy elsewhere would turn a
wider fence stale) plus a control count of the new text, and names an out-of-shard sibling on an
unfenced `escalated` entry. A section or subject shard writes `n/a (section shard; re-checked by
the serial remediator after assembly)`, because assembly deletes the section file its control
names. An insertion-only edit writes `n/a (insertion)`, a deletion-only edit `n/a (deletion)`. The serial
remediator runs the cross-file grep over the assembled files (`s<N>/stories s<N>/epics` after a
files-mode join, never the slot, `shards/` or a record) and re-checks moved cites, after the join.
Every repaired edit owes that grep, so the join prints `SERIAL-REQUIRED: <n>` (repaired entries
with a real edit) beside `ESCALATED-COUNT`, and the procedure dispatches the serial remediator in
every mode when either is above 0. Before this it ran only for an escalation or a multi-file
finding, and in graph s318 `stories-repair-p3` and `stories-elicitation-repair-p1` no serial
remediator ran. `join-remediator-shards.sh`
refuses a missing field in every parts mode, total omission included: the era is the install,
since parts are written fresh by agents reading the installed role file. Only `--sources`, which
checks a record that may span a pull, keeps a PENDING line, binding from the record's first
carrier onward. 0 of graph's 202 s317/s318 shard parts carry the field. The arm's own awk, run
over scratch copies of them, flags 936 entries in 193 parts, with the same run's set-aside count of
1 as its control. Those parts are never re-joined, though: 20 of their 23 dirs already hold a joined record, which a join
refuses to overwrite; the other 3 belong to closed sprints; and no shipped program calls the join.
The field is read in its four forms and no other: a presence reader passed `- siblings: checked`,
and a reader keyed on the word passed any entry whose prose mentions a sibling. The fence is a
`text`-labelled one, a point-in-time record that `validate-artifact-derivations.sh` and the capture
hook never replay: as a `derived` fence its control went STALE the first time a later pass rewrote the
text it counts, and the slot-wide re-run exits 1, "send back to the remediator" (graph's s318 slot
already reads 3316 stale of 4475). The join counts the control once, in parts mode, and refuses a
fence whose text is not in the file it names.

Cost, measured by re-running the join over graph's eight files-mode s317/s318 stories repair
rounds, with a compliant `siblings:` line added to every non-escalated entry: SERIAL-REQUIRED reads
71, 185, 23, 11, 4, 31 and 24 on the seven that join (s317 elicitation, party, adversarial p1, p2;
s318 elicitation, stories p1, p2). That is 349 repaired edits whose cross-file sibling grep the
serial remediator now owes, against the earlier dispatch rule, under which s318 stories-repair-p3
and stories-elicitation-repair-p1 ran no serial remediator. The eighth round, s318 party, refuses on
the known sm-05 set-aside (BL-519), its one true positive; there are 0 false refusals.

Residue (operator ruling: BL-508 closes on the after-join cite re-check, with this recorded): the
`grep -rn -F` line's output is recorded at the edit, never checked at write time (the capture hook
replays only `derived` fences) and never re-run; whether the grepped text is
really the replaced text (the write ledger carries no old_string); a files-mode shard writing the
section-shard form skips the fence, because the four forms are not gated by mode; a `--sources`
record omitting the field everywhere reads PENDING; and a substantive mis-repair whose prose and
pin agree.

## BL-541 — the serial remediator's join is a beat on a record that already exists and is appended to, so it returns on every append and never on completion

Closed in 0.828.0 on a tree receipt, reopened by BL-817. Its decision rule is the step-value ruling, "A step with no measured value goes" (`.claude/rules/operator-rulings.md`).

Closed in 0.828.0 (verified a777c5b4) on a tree receipt, reopened by BL-817. The lease-race half: the beat takes `.beat-inflight` and its EXIT trap directly after the state-dir mkdir, before `--dispatch` resolution, so a beat blocked on the spawn ledger is seen by the stop hook (section 20; receipt below).

**PARTIAL (v0.796.0, verified e3073787; v0.815.0, verified a88f88d4) — the completion signal and its join step shipped; the stop-hook lease-race trace was OPEN here and is superseded by the 0.828.0 close line above.** `_gate-procedures.md` joins the serial and unsharded remediator with `wait-for-deliverable.sh --complete-repair --dispatch <agentId>`, and the auto-handoff and `handoff.md` step 1 split a mixed in-flight set into plain, `--complete` and `--complete-repair` calls. The second subject, whether `ai-dlc-continue.sh`'s `beat_lease_live` misreads a lease a just-returned beat rewrote, was untraced at v0.815.0; the 0.828.0 close line above supersedes that, and the lease is written atomically (`core/scripts/wait-for-deliverable.sh:1202-1204`: a temp file inside `.wait-beats/` renamed over the marker), so the hook never reads a partial line.

**PARTIAL (v0.794.0, verified 8aab009d) — the prose half shipped.** remediator.md: the serial remediator, and the one unsharded remediator, end the record with `repair-complete: serial <pass>` at column 0; a part or shard remediator writes no such line.

**DEFECT (efficiency).** `_gate-procedures.md:975` joins a repair with `scripts/ai-dlc/wait-for-deliverable.sh <repair_record_path>`. For the serial cross-section or cross-part remediator, that path is the JOINED record, which exists before the dispatch, and the remediator APPENDS its entries to it (`:940-942`). The plain predicate, "non-empty and written since the join armed", is therefore met by the first append and by every one after it. `--complete` cannot help: it keys on a last line beginning `seat-complete:`, and a repair record carries none (`wait-for-deliverable.sh:254-312`). So nothing distinguishes a serial remediator that has finished from one that has written one entry.

Measured in graph s319 lead session `62eadbbe-59c3-436d-bf7c-931ebc09ecba`, 23:54Z to 00:04Z: 21 `wait-for-deliverable.sh` invocations on `s319/requirements-party-repair.md` and two lead-made sentinel files. 9 were plain `--since <ts>`, 6 used `--reset --since`, and two waited on sentinels the remediator would never write, so they could only time out. Each return woke a ~300K-token lead turn (BL-538). The lead diagnosed it itself ("each beat returns as soon as the remediator writes again") but had no correct form to arm.

The stop hook also fired "NO LIVE WAIT-BEAT IS ARMED" at 00:00:49Z, seconds after the lead armed beat `bcd634p7x`. That repeats 23:13:02Z, when the lead read `.beat-inflight` five seconds later as holding a future epoch. Both are consistent with `ai-dlc-continue.sh`'s lease test (`beat_lease_live`, `core/hooks/ai-dlc-continue.sh:169`) misreading a lease a just-returned beat rewrote. Neither is proven, because the marker may have cleared between the hook and the read.

Owed: a completion signal the serial remediator writes last (a terminal line in its appended block that the beat can key on, as `seat-complete:` does for seats), and a step that tells the lead to arm `--complete`-style on it; or a join on the agent's own completion notification instead of a file. Separately, trace whether the stop hook's lease read can race a beat's own marker rewrite.

Owed, the mechanism left to the builder: partition the SERIAL-REQUIRED items by the parts they touch, so disjoint sets run as parallel serial lanes and each lane keeps the serial guarantee within its own set. A fixture arm (or receipt): a seeded join whose two disjoint item sets dispatch to two lanes, while an overlapping pair stays in one lane.

Measured input for the partition, graph-watch, batch 238. These figures come from the graph watcher's scratch run of `core/scripts/serial-remediation-worklist.sh` over s319's stories party repair, relayed by the batch-238 lead; this filing did not re-measure them. The run's SUMMARY read `files 19 replaced 115 hits 135 moved-cites 1`, over 19 parts and 148 SERIAL-REQUIRED entries. Taking the parts each item touches as edges, the lane components are: edit only, 19; edit ∪ MOVED-CITE, 18; edit ∪ HIT, 1. One boilerplate line merges every lane: the sprint-title `architecture_refs` line that every story carries (`story-2-1:8-10`, hunk `6.md#F-9`), which HITs line 9 of 18 other stories. On this corpus, a partition on HIT edges therefore yields one lane, the status quo, unless a HIT on a line common to all parts is excluded from the edge set. The builder must decide whether such a common-line HIT can be excluded safely, or must be routed as a single fan-in item.

Built (batch 240, R2): lanes are keyed on FILES from each part's `edit:` set, joined only by MOVED-CITE edges from the worklist the join now runs after a sections or subject assembly (`--keep`); a HIT or escalation reaching two or more lanes is one FANIN item, so the common-line HIT is routed to the fan-in and never excluded. Lanes run as a second parts-mode round through the same join (`--artifact <name>-serial`), and `--escalations`/`--sources` read that round's record after round one's.

D3: `fp_open` ignores the `source:` lines of every shard section in the first record passed, which is round one's own, so a shard that folds a routed token into its own repaired entry acquits nothing; a later record's `source:` covers, and so do entries appended to the first record past its last shard section (the join writes that section as the line count of its shard file; a LANE-COUNT 0, seats-x-parts or requirements-subject round appends there). **Population, derived.** The fixtures still to convert are the rows of `scripts/fixture-inprocess-allowlist.txt`, which BL-879 seeds once from the tree and which only shrinks. Never hand-list them here; read the allowlist.

**Batches.** Group the allowlisted fixtures by shared subject script: build the graph whose edges join a fixture to every script it runs, taken from its `invocations.decl` subject rows and from its calls into `core/scripts/`, `core/hooks/`, `core/skills/` and `scripts/`. A batch is one connected component of that graph, so two sessions never change the same script in parallel. One session owns a component until every fixture in it is converted. Order the components by the summed loaded seconds of their fixtures in `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/ai-dlc-fixture-durations`, costliest first. The durations decide ORDER only, never membership.

**Done, per fixture.**

1. Every cell runs in process. The only command-line runs left are one per distinct CLI outcome of the subject, each with an equivalence cell proving the in-process answer is byte-identical to the command-line answer (stdout, stderr and exit code) on a refusing input and on a passing input that differ.

The tip adversary ruled that the SKIP cannot be reached over a readable subject that is wrapped but broken. A broken body still carries both halves, so the fixture runs and FAILs. Its two sides read equal, so that hypothesis is not supported, which is not evidence that the logger is sound on this fixture.
- backlog-receipt-binding is build-once, cited by text: its `seed()` builds a template once. Its build count is OWED; it needs a counted run at push time, since the fixture is not run outside a push.

A logger reading stands only where a plain run of the same unit agrees with it. A unit whose arms background a function gets the plain pair or a by-text citation, never the logger alone.

An instrument that shadows a command name changes what `command -v` answers, so a fixture that captures its real tool that way runs a different program. That caused this batch's 1,724-process burst and the hang. And a logger keyed on `git init` and `cp -R` cannot see a world built with `mkdir` and `printf`, so its "0 repeats" is a floor, not a count.

Deviations the hands reported:
- **Not using `lib/inproc.sh`.** P2 reads `. "$1"` as an unrouted drive or as an unpaired source wherever a fixture declares an unguarded bash subject. So these fixtures source the subject in a stripped subshell paired with `fx_inproc`. Superseded since 0.1165.0 (BL-1164): P2 exempts `lib/inproc.sh`'s own source lines at the library (the INPX block of `scripts/validate-fixture-invocations.sh`) and judges each `inproc_load`/`inproc_run` call instead; the remaining cause is a call operand no literal path resolves in such a fixture (`:1013`, unpaired by `:1026`), which a literal-tail operand (`"${1%/*}/<subject>"`) removes. All of the fixtures below are on `inproc_run`:
  - layer-title-join;
  - retired-layer-token, through its own `rlt_run`, which copies `inproc_run`'s clean-up and so departs from contract clause C8; its `vec()` now names its 17 predicates literally;

- **Rotate and size start reverify as a program.** backlog-ledger and backlog-size-ceiling answer that start through a fixture-local `bash` shim. The shim sources reverify in a subshell reset to fresh-bash state and calls `brv_main`, and its output is byte-identical to the CLI.

- **Pre-wrap gate.** Every shipping converted fixture carries the pre-wrap consumer gate. owed-derivations answers a writer that carries neither wrap half with SKIP and then `fx_skip_exit` before any assertion.

Deviations the hands reported:
- **Not using `lib/inproc.sh` because of P2.** advisor-gate-deny, updater-session-signals and gate-resume declare unguarded bash hooks as `!` inputs. So they source the subject in a subshell paired with `fx_inproc`, BL-1164's shape: `grep -c 'lib/inproc.sh'` reads 0 in each `inputs.decl`, against 1 for subagent-probe. Each checks the hook's two wrap halves before sourcing it. Corrected in batch 259 C3b: BL-1164 was PARTIAL on this tree, not LANDED, and P2 never judged `lib/inproc.sh`'s own source lines here (they are exempt at the library since C2). The measured cause was the call operand: `inproc_run "$_f"`, `"$1"` or `"$HOOK"` resolves to no literal path, and in a fixture declaring an unguarded subject `scripts/validate-fixture-invocations.sh:1013` reads that as a drive and `:1026` leaves it unpaired. C3b moved all three onto `inproc_load`/`inproc_run` with literal-tail operands (BL-1164, LANDED).
- **Not using `lib/inproc.sh` for another reason.** fixture-git-env-seam's `vf_ip` (unit g) uses a subshell source because, at 747f89054, declaring the library let the inner setup-config-drift run past its own source and failed J7.
- **Local helpers.** release-version-triple's `rv_ip` sources the validator in a subshell paired with `fx_inproc` and calls `rv_main`. plan-rotate's `vps_ip` names `$VPS` as `INPROC_LOADED` for its call (`core/fixtures/plan-rotate/run.sh:787-789`), so the validator runs in process.
- **readset-skip.** Its 20 deriver starts are slot-world.sh's derivers A and B. They stay processes because the slot holder is the deriver's `$$` and its reap is by process group. They are tagged `FXCELL=<SW_CELL>.<scenario>[.b]` and declared `e2e`.
- **readset-skip-b.** Its 45 stub derivers now sit at the consumer layout path (`LT_DVP`), which `readset_deriver_path` resolves first, so its subject row goes 45 -> 0. The dist-layout resolution is still driven by the `seed_lt` worlds.
- **invariant-index.** It drops its `scripts/validate-enforcement-map.sh` `inputs.decl` row: every world is a seeded copy that carries its own validator.
- **mutation-red-replay.** The `cli-hard` cell compares the stderr line carrying the validator's own mktemp backup path after that path is replaced by a token.
- **h2-attest-scripts-dir.** `--attest` has no cli cell, because its stdout carries a `date -u` stamp to the second.
- **vocabulary-index.** The STALE outcome has no cli cell: `cells.decl` holds cli-ok, cli-missing and cli-usage, and the stale index is asserted in process (`run.sh:602`).
- **census-hermetic-coverage.** The census pool starts `bash <census> --pair` through xargs, which an in-process subshell cannot hold. So a bash shim that run.sh writes first on the PATH answers that argv by sourcing the new `pair-worker.sh` (tracked 100755). The eqv byte compare replaces each side's mktemp'd work dir with `<WORK>`.
- **transient-ignore-block.** The wrap returns early only when the script is SOURCED. Run as text (`bash -c "$(cat f)"`), it does NOT return early: the guard's `return` prints one stderr line, and the body runs with stdout and exit equal to base, with or without `--root`. `core/skills/ai-dlc-update/reconcile/apply.sh:3846` is `bash "$TI_RENDERER" --check --root "$CONSUMER"`, a FILE run, which is neither. Unit k's hand differential, base vs tip copies at `scripts/ai-dlc/`, read 14/14 SAME, the apply.sh:3846 shape included.
- **Seeded worlds** are built once and copied in the two acknowledge fixtures and the two renderer fixtures.

Before the integration check, h2-attest-scripts-dir had none, and advisor-gate-deny, subagent-probe, route-read-required and updater-session-signals FAILED against a hook that lacked the wrap. - The record is `$GITDIR/ai-dlc-fixture-skips.log`. It is written only when `[ -n "$PUSH_LINES" ] && [ "$POOL_DEPTH_IN" -eq 0 ]` and a builtin `: >>` writability test passes (otherwise one `..` line). Header: `<stamp>\tPUSH\t<hook pid>\t<local shas comma-joined>\t<HEAD tree>\t<suite key or ->\t<dist=l/r/s consumer=l/r/s | reason>`. Skip row: `<stamp>\tSKIP\t<hook pid>\t<layout>\t<fixture>\t<class or key>\t<state>`.
- The writer sits inside `readset_pending_recorded`'s awk (FIXTURE_POOL, both hooks identical, I66; new `skips_stamp`, `skips_flush`, `skips_header`). Its population is the skip rows of `.kdec` and of `.cl/.kdec` that have no verdict file. Covered: a whole-suite key HIT (one `*` line), the read-set skip (dist), the consumer-layout pass, verdict-store skips (class v), the pre-suite key skip (layout `presuite`), a header-only return (no-kdec), the invalidation guard, cl-refused, empty-suite, cl-tree-mktemp and cl-tree-build. `AI_DLC_FIXTURE_NO_SKIP=1` reaches no-kdec (header only). The stamp reuses `key_log`'s date (no fork on a HIT) and each push adds one `git rev-parse` for the tree. The consumer hook carries the I66 lines but nothing sets `SKIPS_LOG` there, so a consumer's push writes nothing. Growth: one header plus the skip lines per push, no rotation.

## BL-974 — a record-format error in a shard or repair part is found by the lead's join, so one malformed line costs a resume round trip

**DEFECT (efficiency).** An adversary or remediator seals its part, the lead runs the merge or join, the join refuses the part on one line (an `artifact_sha:` stem in the provenance block, an `edit:` line that does not resolve, a coverage gap in the part record), and the lead resumes the finished agent to correct that line. Population for every figure: graph's Claude Code transcripts, 151 lead and 6,018 subagent, read only, window end 2026-11-11T10:30:00Z, extracted by `docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s317-s320/scripts/extract.py` with the s321/s322 edge at 2026-11-09T00:00:00Z; s322 is partial (planning complete, 3 of 8 stories done). In-session time only; handoff gaps are excluded by ruling. Resume messages to finished subagents, classified by their text: s321 13 join or merge refusals with 4.5 agent-hours of idle before the resume (21 minutes each); s322 16 with 11.2 agent-hours (42 minutes each). Each loop is also a lead turn to diagnose, a message, and a second join. Dollars: about $30 across the 29 loops, estimated at about $1 a resume; not measured per loop. The idle is agent idle, an upper bound on wall clock, because other agents may run meanwhile. Instances: s322 `requirements-p2/6.md` (`artifact_sha:` stem), s322 `requirements-repair-p1/1.md` (`edit:` line of F-1), s321 `stories-party-repair-p1/15.md` (coverage gap at line 112).

Fix direction, not built: the writer runs the join's own per-part check before it seals, so the refusal reaches the agent while it still holds the context. `--check-part` exists and the s322 agents ran it clean before the join refused them, so the gap is the difference between what `--check-part` checks and what the join and merge refuse. Close that difference in the per-part check; do not add a second checker. False-positive set and consumer cost unmeasured.

Baseline: s321
Step: requirements
Expected movement: join and merge refusals that end in a resume of the writing agent fall from 13 (s321) and 16 (s322 partial) a sprint to 2 or fewer, and no part that passed its own per-part check is refused by the join for a format reason.

Decision rule: the step-value ruling, "A step with no measured value goes" (`.claude/rules/operator-rulings.md`). Related: BL-804 (the `derivations: not replayed` refusal, one member of this class), BL-532, BL-544.

Receipt: `verify: manual`; closes on an `Outcome measured:` line counting refusal resumes on a graph sprint. What else would satisfy a weaker receipt: a fixture showing `--check-part` refuses one of the three named lines passes while the other refusal classes stay join-only. What this does not establish: which refusal classes exist beyond the three instances read; the 29 were counted by message text and not enumerated by class.

Provenance: batch 255 efficiency analysis (branch b255-efficiency-analysis), measured by the analysis session; id allocated by lead ai-dlc-7f.

## BL-972 — a pending AskUserQuestion holds the lead, so a lane that finishes during the question waits for the answer

**DEFECT (efficiency).** Population for every figure: graph's Claude Code lead transcripts and their subagent transcripts, read only, to 2026-11-11T10:30:00Z: 247 asks over s317–s322, with sprints from the `EDGES` in `docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s317-s320/scripts/extract.py`. s322 is partial. In-session time only; handoff gaps are excluded by ruling. Measured by `docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s317-s322/scripts/ask_split.py` (output `docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s317-s322/out/ask_split.txt`). Its per-sprint call counts and hours equal `operator_asks.py`'s for s317–s321. A wait is FINISHED-INSIDE when a subagent of the same lead session, started before the ask, wrote its last record during it. FINISHED-INSIDE minutes of all answer-wait minutes: s317 197 of 398, s318 271 of 811, s319 164 of 1113, s320 791 of 3052 (26%), s321 164 of 1576 (10%), s322 20 of 537. Those lanes are not joined or followed while the question is open. 290 task notifications were enqueued inside 77 of the 247 asks: 133 from agents, the rest from background Bash and Monitor. Every FINISHED-INSIDE ask has at least one agent notification. Yet no notification-carrying attachment or user record, and no lead assistant record, falls between any question and its answer (`DLV-INSIDE` 0, `ACT-INSIDE` 0). The script's self-probe proves both counters fire on a seeded inside record and stay at 0 on a same-message near-miss. 67 queue `remove` records do fall inside, and no record shows the lead's model receiving those before the answer. Control, asserted in the script: BL-841's 10-27 06:57Z ask scores FINISHED-INSIDE (95 min; two subagents finished inside it). Dollars: $0, a wait bills nothing.

The ceiling, stated so the entry is not read as owning the whole 26.3 h. The figure that names this defect is FINISHED-INSIDE. Most of s321's largest bucket, NONE-RUNNING, 1086 of 1576 minutes (69%), is deploy-validate asks with nothing running: 940 minutes, including the 645-minute "Router PUT" and the 264-minute "Merge #1305". These are operator actions on the serial deploy path, and no lead-side mechanism shortens an operator's answer. FINISHED-INSIDE also UNDERCOUNTS, in two ways. An agent that finished inside a wait and was resumed later has its last record after the ask: 3 asks outside FINISHED-INSIDE (397 min, all sprints) carry an enqueued agent `finished` notification. And background Bash and Monitor completions held by an ask are not bucketed at all. A lead that keeps working while a question is open could also dispatch ready lanes inside a wait of any bucket, and no transcript says where those were.

**Correction (2026-11-11, b255 F4b).** `ask_split.py` now deduplicates asks by `tool_use` id, so one s321 ask (23.9 min) that sits in two lead files is counted once. Under the deduplicated script the population above reads 246 asks, and s321 reads 1552 min with NONE-RUNNING 1063 and deploy-validate 916, against 247, 1576, 1086 and 940. FINISHED-INSIDE 164 is unchanged in minutes, and its share reads 164 of 1552 (11%) where the s321 figure above says 164 of 1576 (10%); NONE-RUNNING reads 1063 of 1552 (68%) where the ceiling paragraph says 1086 of 1576 (69%); any reading of s321's FINISHED-INSIDE minutes is therefore against 164 of 1552. The receipt's s321 ask-count baseline is `ask_split.py`'s deduplicated 56, not `operator_asks.py`'s 57. The two tools differ by that one duplicated row, so a closer must compare the ask count only within `ask_split.py`'s output, never across the two tools, and a count of 56 against 57 is not a fall in asks.

Fix direction, built at batch 256 (the Progress paragraph below). The contact shape is ruled. Immediately before the question, the lead joins every finished lane and dispatches every lane the question does not hold. The question itself goes out at once, in `AskUserQuestion`, unchanged. Asking in prose instead of the tool is NOT this fix: Rule 11(a) requires `AskUserQuestion` for an ambiguity question, and `core/hooks/ai-dlc-continue.sh:1637` records the measured failure of the prose form (the operator: "you haven't asked any question ... buried in the transcript"). No variant may suppress, batch away, defer or hold back a question. The ask count is no longer a close condition: a fall is not credited to dispatch-then-ask, and none is required (batch 259 operator choice: design choices decided on the lead's recommendation are expected to lower it); the Receipt below states the hand reading that replaces it. Whether the harness offers a non-blocking ask is unmeasured; BL-994 owns that probe.

**Progress (batch 256).** Operator ruling, batch 256, on contact shape: option 1, "dispatch, then ask". Immediately before each `AskUserQuestion`, the lead joins every finished lane and dispatches every lane the question does not hold, then asks at once in `AskUserQuestion`, unchanged. Option 2 (a non-blocking ask) and option 3 (accept the hold) were not chosen; option 2's harness question is filed as BL-994. Landed: `core/skills/ai-dlc/SKILL.md` gains the subsection `#### Operator decisions: dispatch, then ask (Rule 11(a))`, and Rule 11(a) item (4) now cites it. `core/fixtures/process-rule-pins/run.sh` pins that subsection's paragraph with the `exact`-mode row `r11a-dispatch-ask`, and its deferral mutants `r11a-dispatch-ask-D1` (the paragraph replaced by "Before every `AskUserQuestion`, wait until every running lane has finished, join them, then ask.") and `r11a-dispatch-ask-D2` (the drain sentence "Ask once every running lane has finished." appended) are both killed. The pin's `exact` row also requires its subsection to hold exactly one paragraph, so a drain paragraph added beside it fails the pin too. `docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s317-s322/scripts/ask_split.py` gains the HELD-AT-ASK, DISPATCHED-AT-ASK and ADJ-DISPATCH columns that the Receipt below reads. Two contract-adversary findings, which are the adversary's figures and are not re-derived here. First, item (4) of Rule 11(a) ("Dispatch ready actions on free lanes ...") was already live in graph's installed engine through s321, which ran 0.969.0 to 0.1028.0. Second, at all 10 of s321's FINISHED-INSIDE asks nothing was visibly held: the lanes finished after the question went out, so a join before the ask cannot reach them. ACT-INSIDE is dropped as the close key. It counts lead records positioned while the ask's tool_result is pending (`ask_split.py`'s ACT counter), so under a blocking ask a compliant lead reads 0 by construction, and DLV-INSIDE is 0 on every baseline ask. The literal first-draft HELD and DISPATCHED definitions failed too. Tail-only lanes scored as dispatched; DISPATCHED now opens a lane only at a harness-confirmed dispatch or resume and closes it at the agent's terminal notice, with no subagent record timestamp and no 300 s tail. Race notices scored as held; HELD now counts only an agent notice enqueued before the `api-request` record that began the ask's response, and one enqueued after it is a race and is not held. Known limits of the pin: inside its subsection the `exact` row does not catch a drain instruction written as a `#####` sub-heading, because headings are skipped; one inside a fenced block; or one inside an HTML comment, because fences and comments are invisible to every test. The lead model reads raw markdown, so these are real survivors; closing them changes the fixture's grammar for every pin, which is a separate change.

A row exists only from the operator's answer to a proposal whose text carries `Standing ruling proposal: match=<match>; class=<class>` (`<match>` exactly the row's `match:`; `<class>` `pipeline-family` or `update-family`, both declared in the schema); `source:` cites that answer's entry in the consumer's `_bmad-output/operator-answers-history.md`, or a pending-decision reply's entry in `_bmad-output/operator-requests-history.md` whose DP entry carries the same marker, `ruling:` is the answer verbatim, and `check` reports any other row as unsourced. A proposal naming a class of the sort's Outside list (`scope-confirmation`, `gate-stop`, `operator-relief`, `tier1`, `locked-requirement`, `step-reserved`), no class or an unknown class never becomes a row, so a row never decides those questions. The engine ships an empty record and never becomes the source of a ruling. A PreToolUse hook on `AskUserQuestion` consults the record: a question whose header equals an active row's `match:` is denied, the reason citing the row, until its text carries `not SR-<n>: <reason>` (any run of spaces after the colon); the hook is stateless and holds no memory of an earlier denial; the lead then records a Rule 12 Tier 2 `DECIDED_AUTONOMOUSLY` entry citing the row.
