## BL-1030 — gate 1 has no zero-seat GATE1-SKIP answer after a gate-3 rework, so a records-only rework that gate 3 did not ask to re-review would still dispatch a gate-1 seat

**NOTE (efficiency).** OPEN. Filed 2026-11-13. The second subject of BL-844's title, "a gate-3 rework re-runs gates 1 and 2", split out when BL-844 closed on its gate-2 subject. A gate-1 pass M >= 2 does ask about its delta: `core/scripts/gate-transition.sh` runs `partition-review-diff.sh --route` (`:317`, a one-seat record-only route) and `--narrow` (`:326`). What gate 1 lacks is a zero-seat answer. The `--gate1-rerun` question that records GATE1-SKIP and dispatches no gate-1 seat is asked only in the Rule A block (`:393`-`:397`), when a gate-2 pass M >= 2 opens, so a gate-1 plan opened after a gate-3 rework always dispatches at least one seat.

First reading (batch 257), by `docs/analysis/bl844-gate2-route-seats/derive-g3.sh` (output `out-g3.txt` beside it) at graph `main` c8ab65397, identical at 1449b5c72 apart from the ref line. Population, derived from the `-g3-p<M>.plan` listings: every story with a gate-3 plan at pass >= 2, s321 1-4 and 2-4 and s322 1, 3, 4, 6 and 8, so 9 gate-3 reworks (s320 has no gate plans). Each gate-1 and gate-2 plan is joined to its review file by `reviewed-sha:`.

Classification of each seat, from its review file, first rule that holds: (c) a gate-3 remedy, when the review's text before its `## Verdict` heading names gate 3 and a `Check <n>` (for example "It exists because gate-3 Check 19 FAILed pass 1"); (b) a same-gate re-review, when the same gate's previous pass reads NEEDS_REWORK; (a) a re-run, otherwise. Class (a) is this entry's subject.

Order and the tie convention: by the committer time t of the commit each plan's `sha:` names (plan and review files were committed in one batch per sprint, so their own commit times order nothing). Rework M owns a class (a) or (b) plan with t(g3 p<M-1>) < t <= t(g3 p<M>), and a class (c) plan with t(g3 p<M-1>) <= t < t(g3 p<M>). A remedy runs at the very sha the failed gate-3 pass judged, with no new commit, so the tie is broken by the remedy citation, never by time. The first version of this reading used the time window alone; it dropped s322 1 g1 p2 and mis-assigned s322 3 g1 p4, and its "6 of the 9 reworks re-ran neither gate" and "12 seats" are withdrawn.

Controls in the same run: s322 1 g1 p2 (a remedy at gate-3 p1's own sha) classifies (c), and s322 3 g1 p2 (the partitioned gate-1 pass after gate-3 p1) classifies (a); a seeded remedy line reads 1 before the verdict heading and 0 after it; the impossible story `ZZNOPE-8f3a1q` joins 0 plans; `GATE1-RERUN` appears in 0 graph plans and `GATE1-SKIP` in 18 (s321 12, s322 6), and the matcher reads a seeded `gate: rerun` / `route: rerun GATE1-RERUN:` plan, the form `core/fixtures/gate-transition/run.sh` asserts.

| Gate-3 rework | Seats that follow (class, non-record paths since the same gate's previous pass) | (a) | (b) | (c) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| s321 1-4 p2, s321 2-4 p2, s322 6 p2 | none | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| s322 1 p2 | g1 p2 record-only (c, 0) | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| s322 1 p3 | g1 p3 serial, 0 reviewable files (c, 0) | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| s322 3 p2 | g1 p2 partitioned, 5 seats (a, 105); g1 p3 serial (b, 1); g2 p2 serial, records GATE1-SKIP (a, 1) | 6 | 1 | 0 |
| s322 3 p3 | g1 p4 serial (c, 0) | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| s322 4 p2 | g1 p2 serial (c, 1); g1 p3 serial (b, 3); g2 p3 serial (a, 4); g2 p4 record-only (b, 0) | 1 | 2 | 1 |
| s322 8 p2 | g1 p4 serial (c, 1) | 0 | 0 | 1 |

Totals: 15 seats after the 9 reworks, (a) 7, (b) 3, (c) 5; 3 reworks re-ran neither gate. Every class (a) seat reviewed a delta carrying code or test paths since the same gate's previous pass: s322 3 g1 p2 105 paths, s322 4 g2 p3 4 (`meta-gate.sh`, its test `test-s239-2-check26-discrimination.sh`, and two extension docs, `gate-validation-domain.md` and `deploy-validate-domain.md`), and s322 3 g2 p2 1 path, `server/test_live_smoke.py`, whose diff (`git diff c6ebe5c96d 9c572624c0`) changes executable test lines (`wait_until` and a `wait_for` call), not only docstrings. So 0 class (a) seats ran over a records-only delta. Every records-only gate-1 seat after a rework (s322 1 g1 p2 and p3, s322 3 g1 p4) was a class (c) remedy gate 3 asked for: a skip keyed on the delta alone would have removed all 3 and no other seat.

Verdict on the subject: NOT discharged as a mechanism, and no cost measured. Gate 1 still has no zero-seat answer after a gate-3 rework, but s321 and s322 hold no discriminating case: 0 class (a) seats over a records-only delta. That zero is a missing input, not an acquittal.

What ships, the same edit in `.githooks/pre-push` and `core/git-hooks/pre-push` (I66), one `# VS-IDENTITY 1` row in each:
- readset_manifest's existing per-path loop also writes `.modes`, `<path>\t<tag>` for each admitted path that is not a plain regular file: `x` for an executable file, `l:<readlink target>` for a symlink. Builtins only, plus one `readlink` per symlink (0 tracked today). `.now` and the admitted path set are unchanged.
- Every per-fixture key record readset_keys composes carries `#modes v1` and one `#mode\t<path>\t<tag>` line per non-plain file key, ahead of its rows; the publish (readset_keys_write, cl_publish) puts `#pending` above them, so `#pending` stays line 4. readset_key_records reads both lines; readset_key_rows and readset_vs_want drop them as header lines, so no key row, `.dkeys` row, digest input or store body changes, and hermetic-run.sh is unchanged. The side-record hash, the twin skip's `rows()`, ps_rowkey and invalidation-guard.sh already skip `#` lines.
- The decision: for a record with `#modes v1`, a file key present at both times whose tag differs from its recorded tag (absent = plain) runs the fixture as `mode changed <path>`, class `x`. It outranks a content change, because readset_verdicts (`$4 == "k" || "u" || "s"`), the consumer twin skip and the side-record skip (`$4 == "k"`) and invalidation-guard.sh (`$4 == "k"`) clear or judge other letters only, so a stored pass, which is keyed on content alone, never clears a mode change measured against the fixture's last PUBLISHED record. A key absent from that record, or recorded there as `-`, gets no mode compare. Under the consumer layout the compare runs inside the installed tree against that layout's own record (`sens()` is unchanged: install.sh's `chmod +x` lines set the installed modes before any key is taken, so a mode they give a file is part of every record of that tree and moves no unit between pushes of the same install).
- THE ADOPTION WINDOW, a bounded acquittal of what existed before W. A record without `#modes v1` (written before W) adopts the present modes and types: when nothing else runs the fixture it skips, class `a`, and is republished through `.k.always` (both builders) with the header, announced as `read-set modes: <n> record(s) ...`. So a mode or type change made before a fixture's first W-era record exists is adopted once, without a run. A record stays header-less, and so stays adoptable, until a push publishes a record for that fixture: on a green or a red push every record of a fixture that passed, every `a`/`v`/`m`/`b` republish and every distribution store skip is written with the header.
- ONE-TIME windows, each closed by the next push that publishes the record: a fixture that went red, every record of a killed push, every record of a push refused before dispatch (consumer layout refused, invalidation-guard FAIL), and every record of a whole-suite content-key HIT, which takes no key decision. `scripts/suite-content-key.sh` hashes the exec bits and the symlink targets, so a mode or type change ends the HIT.
- AN OPEN WINDOW, lasting until the unit runs (CLOSED by owed item D1, built in batch 268 cluster R; see the `**PARTIAL (v0.1253.0).**` paragraph below, which also corrects this bullet's re-adoption claim: such a unit did not re-adopt, it stayed header-less and uncompared): an `<fx>@consumer` unit skipped by the twin rule (`d`) or by a side record (`h`). Neither publishes a record (`.k.always` lists only `v`/`m`/`b`/`a`). While it was header-less, a mode change to its installed copy was caught only when the distribution twin itself ran under class `x`, which takes away the `d` skip; an `h` skip does not read the twin and was not caught. The P5 run had 25 `d` units and 0 `h` units on the real store.
- NOT DONE: presuite keys (`ps_select`) get no mode state: the pre-suite pass sets READSET_NOMODES, so its records and decisions are byte-for-byte as before. A push running a hook from before W, at the same time as W pushes, rewrites a record without its `#modes v1` and `#mode` lines, because its writer does not know them; the next W push then adopts that record again. A file keyed only through a span row (`<path>#<NAME>`) has no mode compare. Classes `x` and `a` are asserted by owed item D2, built in batch 268 cluster R; see the `**PARTIAL (v0.1253.0).**` paragraph below.
- UNCOVERED: a key absent from the record or recorded there as `-` gets no mode compare; seeded keys get none; a mode change on a symlink's target is not seen (the tag records the link's target path, not the target's mode).
- Measured (commit message of this change): P1 republish then `chmod -x` runs core-write-guard, core-script-boundary and upstream-routing as `mode changed core/hooks/ai-dlc-core-guard.sh`, `x`; with the compare removed core-write-guard skips. P2 a symlink swap runs, the mutant skips. P3 touch and a same-bytes rewrite skip. P4 a content append to apply-drift-refile runs under both hooks. P5 the dispatch set against the real store is identical under the base and the W hook (46 run, CONSUMER 28); the only difference is 160 plain skips reading `a`. P6 a one-file docs change: identical dispatch and identical PATH-resolved exec counts. P7 invalidation-guard `--predict` after the chmod: no FAIL. ## BL-1152 — P2 cannot see an in-process call of an UNGUARDED subject's functions after its counted source (the B route)

**DEFECT.** OPEN. Filed 2026-11-16. Owner: `scripts/validate-fixture-invocations.sh` P2 (`FXC_P2_AWK`, the counting unit and `fxc_guarded`); `core/fixtures/lib/mutant.sh` (the comment item below).

P2 counts an UNGUARDED subject with a shebang per SOURCE. After that source, a fixture can call the subject's functions any number of times, and P2 counts none of those calls, so they reach no `inproc:` row. The header of `scripts/validate-fixture-invocations.sh` names this the B route and calls it "the LARGER open route". The 312 call sites quoted there were measured on main 62a88119c; 221 of them were in a since-deleted fixture.

Re-measured on 99c662068 (0.1149.0) with a scratch variant of the shipping validator, run from inside a clean worktree of that commit. In the variant, `fxc_guarded` prints `G` for every subject whose first line opens `#!` and logs each file it flips. `bash scripts/validate-fixture-inprocess.sh` then lists, as OWED, every call of a flipped subject's column-0 function. That is the B route as P2 would count it under the per-CALL unit.
- 147 rows over 33 sites in 5 fixtures. Every one is a call of a `core/git-hooks/pre-push` function: 36 rows in each of readset-skip, -b, -c and -d (30 sites, all in `readset-skip/run.sh`), and 3 in consumer-suite-pool (`consumer-suite-pool/run.sh`, 3 sites).
- The fixtures behind the 312 figure are all gone: backlog-receipt-efficiency, story-evidence-receipts-mutants, story-evidence-smoke-mutants and smoke-surface-ignored-mutants each list 0 times in `git ls-tree -d HEAD core/fixtures/`, against readset-skip once.
- Not separated by this measurement: activation. readset-skip's runner sources an unresolvable operand (`. "$@"`), which activates every subject of the fixture, so some of its 144 rows may be phantoms of the kind BL-982's F8 ruling names (spans and drivers, no pass of the subject).

**PARTIAL (v0.1163.0).** batch 258, C10. Owed item 1 is built; items 2 and 3 stay open. The B route is narrowed, not closed.
- P2 (`scripts/validate-fixture-invocations.sh`) counts an unguarded shebang subject per CALL, additive to its per-source rows; 0 rows lost.
- Cover rule: a paired source covers the one entry call after it, in the same function body or subshell.
- +144 rows, all OWED, in readset-skip, -b, -c and -d (36 each). Reason: activation-only phantoms from readset-skip's unresolvable sources (`pool.sh`, the awk-extracted `lib.sh`, the `pool_span` copies); the spans carry no pass of `core/git-hooks/pre-push` (BL-982's F8 ruling).

**DEFECT.** OPEN. Filed 2026-11-17. Owner: `scripts/validate-fixture-hygiene.sh` H14 and `core/fixtures/*`.

H14 (BL-1153) binds C8 only for a command-position `git init` on a code line. A fixture can build a git world by hand in other ways, and one of them is a bypass of the bound rule: rewriting a hand init through a local wrapper (`g() { git "$@"; }; g init`) clears H14 without adopting `core/fixtures/lib/world.sh`.

The remainder, from the `# H14` header of `scripts/validate-fixture-hygiene.sh` (measured at 619bfde94 by an instrumented copy of the arm's scan, controls: hits on the known `gitq -C … init` and `G init` lines; `core/fixtures` is byte-identical at 4c12abee5, `git diff --stat 619bfde94 4c12abee5` naming no path under it):
- Wrapper-function inits (a command-position word other than git/world_git, followed by `init`): 129 code lines in 29 fixtures at 619bfde94, 19 of them with no H14 row. BOUND by H14's wrapper clause (see the PARTIAL line); 133 lines in 30 fixtures at 747f89054.
- Variable-held git: 2 lines, `"$REAL_GIT" init` at fanout-payload-channel run.sh:182 and fanout-untracked-corpus run.sh:121 (run.sh:156 and :96 at 619bfde94), neither an H14 row (re-derived at 747f89054 by `grep -n 'REAL_GIT" init'`: 2 lines). A named blind route of the wrapper clause.

- Script-string inits: 5 lines (fixture-git-env-seam run.sh:274/297/327, review-shard-merge receipt-bl980.sh:114, shell-portability run.sh:433; the first three were :272/295/325 at 619bfde94).

- `cp -R`/`-r`/`-a` in command position: 311 lines in 82 fixtures, an upper bound (not each copies a git world).

## BL-1174 — the efficiency extractor's segment clock charges an out-of-order record twice, so every published sprint-hours figure is overstated

**DEFECT (efficiency).** OPEN. Filed 2026-11-18. Owner: `docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s317-s320/scripts/extract.py` (`scan()`, the `prev_t` assignment) and every committed output and report derived from its `segs.jsonl`.

`scan()` measured each interval from the previous record whatever its timestamp. A record stamped earlier than its predecessor charged 0, and the next record then charged the whole interval again. `Classer.interval()` in the same file is monotone, which is why `roll.py --classes` prints an "out-of-order overcount" line. s323's transcripts replay a burst of `attachment` records stamped before an operator pause after the record that ends it: in lead 68cf8de7 one 4.73 h pause was charged about fifteen times and requirements read 89.6 h.

Measured with `EXTRACT_MONOTONE_SEGS=1` at pin `2026-11-18T17:54:00Z` (the default-clock s317–s322 `TOTAL` lines at that pin are identical to those at `2026-11-12T14:41:00Z`), pipeline bucket, elapsed hours, published against monotone: s317 80.8 and 72.8; s318 74.8 and 59.6; s319 110.0 and 94.0; s320 117.8 and 99.2; s321 120.5 and 111.0; s322 77.1 and 66.4; s323 to the pin 141.2 and 45.8. s323's four lead sessions span 45.8 h first record to last. Token-equivalent dollars, API dollars and lead calls are equal between the two clocks for every sprint. Source: `docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s323-provisional-b259/out/s323_provisional.txt`.

Shipped in batch 259 (C4b): the opt-in switch `EXTRACT_MONOTONE_SEGS=1`, default off, with `roll.txt` and `roll_classes.txt` at the old pin `cmp`-identical to the committed b259 outputs after the edit; and a dated correction note at the top of the three published reports.

Fix, at the s323-close re-take and once: make the monotone clock the default; regenerate every committed output that reads `segs.jsonl` or `steps.csv` hours under `docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s317-s320/`, `-s317-s322/` and `-s317-s322-b259/`; restate the hours in `pipeline-efficiency-s317-s322.md` and `pipeline-efficiency-s317-s322-b259.md`; re-run `pipeline-efficiency-s317-s318.md`'s own extractor copy, which has the same clock and was not measured; and correct each backlog `Outcome measured:` or progress line that quotes sprint or step hours from the old clock, listing them by entry.

Read (batch 261, C5; tree `c4b7f370a`; extract, spawns and analyze re-run per pin and clock, `EXTRACT_MONOTONE_SEGS=0` reproducing each quoted figure in the same invocation unless marked). The only verdict rule crossed is BL-911 L1378, whose planning-hours band is old clock and was recomputed on the monotone clock. ## BL-1175 — PLANNING, the one entry: planning costs about 40 hours and $900 to $1,300 whatever the sprint is, and every planning-cycle fix is a work item here

**DEFECT (efficiency).** OPEN. Filed 2026-11-18. Owner: `core/skills/ai-dlc/steps/route.md` (the intensity classification, lines 527–543), `core/skills/ai-dlc/SKILL.md` Rule 8 (the intensity table, lines 238–253), and the four planning step files (`carry-over-evaluation.md`, `requirements.md`, `architecture.md`, `stories-test-strategy.md`).

**This is the single entry for the cost of the planning cycle, by operator ruling of 2026-11-18.** No other entry is filed for it. A new planning finding becomes a work item below. BL-1169, BL-1170 and BL-1171 are folded in as work items 3, 4 and 2. There is no target number, by operator ruling of 2026-11-18: gains come from removing waste that an honest reading finds, not from a figure chosen in advance. The entry is done when every work item is shipped or closed on its reading AND a complete graph sprint has been measured against the baseline; it is never split, and an item is never moved to another entry.

### What is wrong

`route.md:531` assigns `full` to any sprint with three or more stories touching service code paths, and `SKILL.md:250–253` gives each tier a minimum cycle per planning artifact. One tier is recorded for the whole sprint. Nothing reads what kind of change a story is, so a story that extends existing behaviour or fixes a bug takes the same four document steps and the same review and repair series as a new subsystem, and one story that needs the full cycle puts every story through it.

Measured on graph, read only, in-session time only, the four planning steps with their gates, on the monotone segment clock (`EXTRACT_MONOTONE_SEGS=1`, BL-1174) with the default clock beside it. The intensity is the `validation_intensity` line of graph's `_bmad-output/pipeline-snapshot.md` at each ref.

| Sprint | Graph ref | Intensity | Stories | Planning h, monotone (old clock) | Less operator wait | Token-eq $ (API $) |
|---|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| s321 | `ec443477d` | `full` | 25 | 40.8 (43.0) | 36.8 | 1,298 (1,279) |
| s322 | `f7e60625b` | `carry-over-single` | 8 | 36.9 (44.0) | 30.0 | 889 (720) |
| s323 | `16fd227d9` | `full` | 18 | 39.6 (133.1) | 27.0 | 1,071 (876) |

Reading on complete s323 (batch 261; pin EXTRACT_WIN_END=2026-11-20T04:20:00Z; monotone clock unless labelled). s321, s322 and s323 are complete. The `(old clock)` column is the default clock before BL-1174 (`EXTRACT_MONOTONE_SEGS=0`); both columns reproduce at the shipped extractor, and s323's 133.1 h is an artifact of that clock. The s323 row was first taken at `e70a344c0` and pin `2026-11-18T17:54:00Z` with the same figures. Source: `docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s323-complete-b261.md` and its `out/` files (`out/s323_complete.txt`).

- The charge does not follow the work. 8, 18 and 25 stories each paid 37 to 41 hours.
- The reduced tier does not reduce it. s322 ran `carry-over-single` and paid 36.9 h and $889.
- Planning is most of a sprint. In s322 it was 36.9 of 66.4 h and $889 of $1,348; implementing all eight stories took 13.0 h and $223.

The planning rounds hold named catches (in s321's stories step, 39 unique survivors in the per-story elicitation shards, including the CRITICAL 17#F-1 on story 4.3, `docs/analysis/step-value-stories-elicitation-s321.md:121`; and 8 in adversarial pass 1, including the CRITICAL 19 F-1 on story 5.2, `docs/analysis/step-value-stories-adversarial-s321.md:194`; corrected in batch 259, C5, from a sentence that gave the elicitation count against the adversarial file), so the work below matches depth to the change and removes no round that holds a catch.

### Work items

Each item states its own acceptance. Items 1 and 2 waited on item 0; items 3 to 6 do not. Item 6 was added in batch 259, C5. What each item shipped or closed on is under "Progress" below.

0. **The reading that sizes items 1 and 2. No code, no new run.** From graph's s321 to s323 planning artifacts and the step-value files: classify each story as carrying a new requirement, a new architecture decision, both or neither; count the surviving requirements-step, architecture-step and stories-step findings raised against each class and against each routing tag. Also read what the requirements and architecture steps' cost scales with (in-scope stories, document parts, shards per pass), because their hours so far do not follow story count: requirements was 11.1, 9.9 and 13.5 h and architecture 10.0, 5.8 and 5.2 h for 25, 8 and 18 stories. That decides what item 1 saves in a mixed sprint. Done when both tables are in this entry.
1. **Tier per story on what the story changes, not per sprint on story count** (`route.md:527–543`, `SKILL.md` Rule 8). A story carrying neither a new requirement nor a new architecture decision does not enter the requirements or architecture review series: those documents name it as out of scope and it enters at the stories step. A sprint made only of such stories runs carry-over evaluation and the stories step. Ships only if item 0 shows such stories hold few or no surviving requirements or architecture findings; otherwise it is closed here with that reading. Ceiling on s323, if no story needed either step: 18.7 h (13.5 + 5.2, of which 6.2 h was operator wait) and $447 ($274 + $173).
2. **Tier the per-story party and elicitation rounds inside the stories step by the routing tag the step already carries** (`stories-test-strategy.md:30`; was BL-1171). Untagged stories take adversarial pass 1 only; capital-path and security-tagged stories keep the full cycle. Ships only if item 0 shows survivors cluster in tagged stories. Estimate: $134 a sprint if 40% of 25 stories are untagged, at s321's $7.49 and $5.96 a story; wall clock moves little because the rounds are parallel.
3. **One readiness run when the first passes, and no file nobody reads** (`architecture.md:262`, `stories-test-strategy.md:18` and `:542`; was BL-1169). Read the three calls' spawns and findings on s321 and s322; a call with no finding that reached a fix goes. The `intent=sprint-planning` output is not produced when nothing consumes its sprint data. Estimate: 0.5 to 1.2 h and $5 to $11 a sprint, on 10 to 20 minutes and $1.50 a call, to be replaced by the measured figures.
4. **The planning-time trace gate that cannot fail moves to sprint review** (`stories-test-strategy.md:677–700`; was BL-1170). At planning, a deterministic check fails on a criterion with no mapped case; the trace runs once at sprint review, where its verdict can read FAIL. Hours and dollars: the planning run's measured cost, read from s321 and s322 before the change. As built in batch 259, C5, the item is a removal only: no AC-to-case check and no sprint-review trace run were added (Progress, item 4).
5. **Pass 2 no wider than what the pass-1 repair changed.** The mechanism is BL-911's and stays there; this item is its planning outcome. On s323 the adversary ran 15 spawns at requirements p1 and 15 at p2, 5 and 5 at architecture, 4, 5 and 4 at carry-over. Join each series' pass-2 width to its changed-part count; if pass 2 is wider than the changed parts plus the cited parts plus one, the defect is reported to BL-911 and fixed there, and this item closes when a sprint shows the narrowed width.
6. **Passes per series** (added batch 259, C5). After pass 1, s321 to s323 ran 28 further adversarial passes. They hold 1 CRITICAL (s321 architecture p4 F-1, introduced by the p3 repair, text written at `architecture-repair-p3.md:373–383`) and 29 first-authored MAJORs (27 of them in s321). Today every MAJOR less the underived ones counts toward NOT_MET (`core/team-roles/adversary.md:441–465`; `validate-adversarial-convergence.sh:706–710`). A MAJOR that a mechanical join places inside the repair made between pass N-1 and pass N stops counting toward NOT_MET; it still gets its targeted fix and a lead check that the convergence validator can see; a CRITICAL always blocks; a finding that cannot be joined blocks. Candidates scored on the record (estimates apportioned by spawns): the partition (b) removes 7 passes, about 4.4 h less operator wait and $97 over the three sprints, losing 0 CRITICAL and 0 first-authored MAJOR, with 20 MAJORs going to targeted fix; a pass cap of 2 removes 15 passes but loses the s321 CRITICAL and 11 first-authored MAJORs, a cap of 3 removes 6 and loses the CRITICAL and 4; candidate (d) is already shipped. The join must read only the previous pass's repair: under an any-earlier-repair join, s321 architecture p3 reads MET and the p4 CRITICAL is lost. Item 6 SHIPS in this release, built in full by operator ruling. Mechanism: the merge snapshots the bytes it reviewed and quotes-joins each CRITICAL/MAJOR against the immediate predecessor pass's snapshot only; a MAJOR is repair-introduced only if ALL its quotes occur exactly once in pass N and 0 times in pass N-1, blocking = major - max(underived, repair_introduced), CRITICAL always blocks, and an unquoted or unjoinable finding blocks. A stem with more than 25% of its lines changed makes every finding blocking, J3 closes repair-introduced keys only as repaired (never deferred), and the gate alone re-derives the count through the merge (arm R). Snapshots are UNTRACKED at `s<N>/adversarial-snapshots/<sha256>` (the directory carries its own `.gitignore`), roughly 270-280 KB per pass per document on disk, never committed. An already-merged pass keeps its recorded count; arm R reports PENDING and does not block, so a lost snapshot degrades to the recorded count and never refuses. A pass merged after its predecessor's snapshot is lost finds every finding unjoinable and blocks. Arm R counts only merge-written passes (those carrying `shard_tool_use_ids:`, as arms B and E do), and a re-merge of an existing pass whose predecessor's snapshot is lost keeps the stored count and answers UNCHANGED. Numbers: measured removal is 0 of 7 passes on today's grammar and 0 of 3 measurable under the ALL rule; the 7 passes, about 4.4 h and $97 over s321-s323 is a CEILING (estimate), and the real joinable share is first measurable on graph's first sprint after the pull, because the quote grammar arrives with the reconcile PR. Calibration of the 25% ceiling (changed share between consecutive passes): s321 architecture p3 to p4 18.2%, s321 test-strategy p4 to p5 10.6%, s323 coe p1 to p2 16.5%, s322 spine p1 to p2 49.7%; the last is over the ceiling, so all its findings stay blocking.

**PARTIAL (v0.1246.0).** Batch 267, cluster Z. Arm P1J's section-shard exception now ties a part to its own block, and the identity rule is filtered by artifact. (a) A triple counts as a part of a shard block only inside that block: the last block ends at its marker line plus the line count of its part file under `shards/<record stem>/` (the extent `fp_open` in `join-remediator-shards.sh` already uses), so a triple the serial remediator appended after the join-written section is a tail and never a part, and a part closes only keys whose shard file is its own block's (zero-padded names compared by number); a block with no shard file closes nothing. ## BL-1187 — every subagent spawn loads the same fixed context before it works: $450 of s323's $1,580 subagent dollars (28%)

**DEFECT (efficiency).** Filed 2026-11-20 (batch 261, C10). Owner: `templates/settings.json.template`, `core/scripts/render-agent-definitions.sh`, `core/team-roles/*.md` and `templates/CLAUDE.md.template`. Source: `docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s323-opportunities-b261.md`, group 6.

Goal: a subagent's first request carries only what its role reads. One done condition: the `Outcome measured:` line on the first complete sprint after items 1 to 5 ship, read against the baseline below.

Population: graph s323 subagents (1,138 spawns), read only, `roll.py` prices, `EXTRACT_WIN_END=2026-11-20T04:20:00Z`. Subagent dollars are 42% cache writes, 40% cache reads and 18% output; the cache hit rate is 96.3%; thinking is $81 in all and no seat runs at high effort, so model and effort bindings are not the lever. A 48.8 KB project-instructions block (graph's `CLAUDE.md`, two rule files, the operator's memory index) loads into 795 spawns in 15 roles, and 0 of them read those files again; `omitClaudeMd` is set for 4 of 19 roles. 1,062 of 1,138 spawns used neither the Skill nor the Agent tool but carry both definitions and a 30 KB skills list.

Restated at the recorded cache-write tier (batch 263 D; `EXTRACT_WIN_END=2026-11-20T04:20:00Z`, `extract.py`, `spawns.py`, `analyze.py`, `roll.py` run once and read from `roll_cachewrite.txt`; BL-1174's batch 263 D paragraph holds the command and population): every subagent record writes five-minute cache (176,161 of 176,705 deduplicated subagent records to the pin have non-zero 5m, none non-zero 1h), so the 2 x input write price under the $450 and the $1,580 was the wrong tier. Subagent dollars for s323: $1,580.2 -> $1,331.8 (-$248.4). The fixed first-request context, recomputed as first-request tokens x (cache-write price + (calls - 1) x cache-read price) over the 1,147 s323 subagent transcripts in the pin (`spawns.jsonl` rows, one record per `message.id`; the same formula at the 2 x input write price reads $452.3 against the $450 above, the control), reads $370.8 at the 5m write price (-$81.5), which is still 28% of $1,331.8; s321 $436.9 -> $357.4 (21.7% of $1,647.3) and s322 $211.6 -> $176.3 (20.1% of $878.8). ## BL-1190 — the engine-update flow hands the model about twelve deterministic scripts to chain and re-read: 4.72, 5.92 and 8.12 lead hours in s321 to s323, outside the sprint figure

**DEFECT (efficiency).** Filed 2026-11-20 (batch 261, C10b). Owner: `core/skills/ai-dlc-update/SKILL.md`, `core/skills/ai-dlc-update/reconcile/` (`emit-report.sh`, `apply.sh`, `layer-drift.sh`, `classify-block.md`) and a new driver under `core/scripts/`. Source: `docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s323-opportunities-b261.md`, section 6.13.

Goal: a pull runs as one program that hands the model only the decisions that need it. One done condition: the `Outcome measured:` line on the first complete sprint after items 1 to 5 ship, read against the baseline below.

Population: lead sessions that loaded `ai-dlc-update` in graph s321 to s323, read only, monotone clock, `EXTRACT_WIN_END=2026-11-20T04:20:00Z`. These sessions are outside each sprint's in-session figure.

Baseline: s321, s322 and s323 had 13, 8 and 8 pulls; lead active 4.72, 5.92 and 8.12 h; elapsed 25.2, 14.1 and 16.4 h (includes waits); lead calls 881, 1,317 and 1,751; compactions 2, 10 and 16; lead API $89.73, $21.38 and $10.93 (s322 and s323 ran a local lead; token-equivalent at the s321 hosted mix $64.39 and $78.92 for s322 and s323); subagents 4, 11 and 8 spawns, $1.64, $3.26 and $2.05. An ask-free pull (5, 3 and 2 of the pulls) costs the lead 0.35, 0.63 and 0.85 h and 64, 147 and 148 calls, about as much as a pull with asks (0.37, 0.80 and 1.07 h): the orchestration drives the cost, not the asks. Every invocation loads a 261,327 B, 3,378-line skill, 32, 21 and 19 loads a sprint (about 65 to 75 thousand tokens at an assumed 3.5 to 4 B per token).

Work list, each measured waste an upper bound on s323 (the part-by-part readings are in the report section):

1. One program runs fetch, the self-update gate (the DEFER decision made from the file set), classify, the detectors once, the report, the branch, the clean applies, the push and the PR. The model is started only on a decisions list: conflict hunks, in-place edits of engine-owned files, extensions not provably additive, and the diagnosis of a red push. Of 46 self-update gate logs in s321 to s323, 34 say SELF-UPDATE-DEFER (nothing done). `emit-report.sh` re-runs every detector and `--verify` and `apply.sh --for-apply --verify` run them again: up to 4 runs per detector per pull, 21 `emit-report` runs for 8 pulls in s323 (mean 2.9 minutes, about 38 minutes a sprint). Classify and detector reading cost the lead 0.46, 0.75 and 1.33 h.
2. Ask only on conflict. The skill contradicts itself: `core/skills/ai-dlc-update/SKILL.md:1968` says to "ask ONE closed question per blocker", while `:2001-2002` says a CONFLICT "is the one place a human is genuinely required" (the reader cited :1966-1967 and :1999-2000; read at the main checkout, the lines are two off). Across s317 to s323 the operator answered 4 of 167 questions other than the recommended or first option; in s321 to s323, 34 of 52 questions were default-accepted (override drift 13, extension still-additive 15, pristine delete 6). Ask wait was 118, 118 and 196 minutes a sprint. The standing-rulings record is BL-972 item 6.
3. The dry run becomes the PR body: no pull ended at the dry run (all 29 went on to apply), the pause between them had a median of about 3 minutes, and the report stage costs the lead 0.82, 1.12 and 2.65 h. `blocker-adjudication-<ts>.md` (120 files in graph) is read by the model and by no program.
4. The semantic classify agents (4, 11 and 8 spawns, $1.64, $3.26 and $2.05) become a script: in all 8 s323 verdicts conflict was 0 and the same `dev.md`, `qa.md` and `deploy-validate.md` recurred every pull; consumer equal to base outside declared setup spans means take theirs, and an agent is dispatched only where it differs.
5. Untangle the always-loaded part of `SKILL.md` and mask or re-inject its sections: after each compaction the first-response gaps total 0.24, 0.46 and 2.08 h (upper bound; each gap also contains real work).

Kept for safety: branch isolation, the conflict stop, deletes only when byte-equal to base, the stop on in-place edits to engine-owned files, the consumer's pre-push suite, and the operator's merge. Not measured: whether a pull-only push (one push per pull) saves the 0.3 to 1.7 h a sprint it bounds; the pre-push suite runs a mean 11.5 to 15.3 minutes, maximum 86.9.

The operator chose on 2026-11-20 to keep the engine-update pace as it is; this entry changes the cost per pull, not how often one is delivered, and dispatches no pull.

Decision rule: the step-value ruling, "A step with no measured value goes" (`.claude/rules/operator-rulings.md`). Related: BL-972 (standing-rulings record), BL-819.

Expected movement: the fix removes the lead hours and calls a pull spends chaining and re-reading scripts; the outcome is read against the baseline above, lead active hours, lead calls and compactions in the update sessions, on the first complete sprint after the items ship.

**PARTIAL (v0.1191.0).** batch 261, E6. Items 1 to 5 are built; the entry stays open on its one done condition, the outcome reading. Sources: `docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s323-opportunities-b261.md` section 6.13 and the runbook `docs/plans/pipeline-efficiency-analysis.md`. Status per item:

1. Built. `core/skills/ai-dlc-update/reconcile/pull.sh` runs fetch, the self-update gate, classify, the detectors once per `apply` invocation (their raw output is reused in-process by the union gate and by `apply.sh`'s pre-write calls while a fingerprint of the inputs holds; a mismatch runs them afresh), the report, the branch, the clean applies, the push and the PR, and hands the model only a decisions list. The "DEFER decision made from the file set" needed no new decision code: the gate already decides it before the hook-script differential runs, exiting 0 at `core/skills/ai-dlc-update/reconcile/self-update-gate.sh:1374-1377` after the file-set DEFER arms at :1176, :1303 and :1369; `pull.sh gate` wraps it. The driver lives in `core/skills/ai-dlc-update/reconcile/pull.sh`, not under `core/scripts/` as the Owner line says: only `core/skills/ai-dlc-update/**` is in the self-update machinery slice (`reconcile/setup-sites.md:99`), so a driver under `core/scripts/` would not land at step 2 of the delivering pull and the re-invoked engine would lack it.
2. Built. A question reaches the operator only for the five families in `core/skills/ai-dlc-update/reconcile/ask-families.tsv`: `conflict-hunk` (a hunk the override merge left), `classify-conflict` (a rule upstream and the consumer changed incompatibly), `blend` (a blend within one block), `delete-consumer-modified` (a removed or relocated file the consumer modified) and `orphaned-unknown` (a file at a relocated path upstream never shipped); the PR merge stays the operator's. That file is the one list the driver and `apply.sh` read and `SKILL.md` renders, and the skill's contradiction is resolved in favour of "a CONFLICT is the one place a human is genuinely required". Clean override merge, still-additive extension, pristine delete, in-place engine edit, red push, the ledger and derivation questions, and setup token with a nearest equivalent no longer ask: each is a model or script decision written to `_bmad-output/ai-dlc-update/pull-decisions.tsv` and rendered into the PR body, so the operator's merge approves it. 4. Built. A CLASSIFY file skips the classify agent only when the acceptance conditions of `apply.sh`'s existing setup-site merge hold, checked without writing; the write goes through that existing path, and every other case dispatches the agent as before.
5. Built. New fixture `reconcile-pull-driver`; `blocker-adjudication-record` is retargeted to the decisions file.

Owed: the outcome reading, on the next complete graph sprint that runs this release, against the baseline above. This release dispatches no pull; when a pull runs is the operator's to schedule.

## BL-1191 — the pipeline-efficiency analysis is not repeatable: its method lived in a session, and its first reading was taken without a per-step pass

**DEFECT (efficiency).** Filed 2026-11-20 (batch 261, C10b). Goal: the analysis can be run again by a later session from the record alone, covers every pipeline step, and cannot be published with a step missing. One done condition: the next run of the analysis under the runbook lands a report that the coverage check accepts, and the check's false-positive measurement over the five earlier reports is recorded. Items 1 to 3 are delivered by the commit that files this entry (batch 261, C10b); item 4 is open.

Baseline: s323, the first reading covered the cross-cutting classes (lead time, tokens, operator asks, late steps, tool runtime) and took no per-step pass; the per-step pass changed published figures: s321 111.0 to 100.1 h, s322 66.4 to 65.2 h, s323 operator wait 17.9 to 20.3 h, requirements 13.5 to 16.9 h, carry-over 11.8 to 8.4 h, sprint review 11.1 to 9.9 h, refused suite launches 261 to 134 distinct (floor).

Work list:

1. The runbook `docs/plans/pipeline-efficiency-analysis.md`: the handoff a later session reads and follows when the operator asks for this analysis again, shaped for `scripts/validate-plan-shape.sh`.
2. The readers committed under `docs/analysis/pipeline-efficiency-s323-opportunities-b261/` with one entry point, its `README.md`.
3. The report's first lines point at the runbook.
4. A push-time check that a pipeline-efficiency report declaring itself under the runbook carries a section per step file, the list derived from the `core/skills/ai-dlc/steps/` directory and never from the manifest's wildcard (`core-manifest.md` declares `steps/*.md`). The false-positive measurement over the five existing pipeline-efficiency reports is a build condition: none of them may fail. It proves coverage, not quality, and says so in its remedy text. It needs its own validator id.

Boundaries and ordering belong to BL-1174: the extractor takes step and gate boundaries from what the pipeline declares and sprint boundaries from the consumer's sprint-close commits, and that change exists before the next sprint's reading is taken. Operator statement, 2026-11-20, as relayed to the builder: "I won't run a graph sprint until all of the backlog items from this analysis are built and pulled to graph." It records the operator's intent about running a sprint; it does not authorize a pull. Consequence for this entry: the next sprint's reading measures the items together.

Decision rule: the step-value ruling, "A step with no measured value goes" (`.claude/rules/operator-rulings.md`). Related: BL-1174, BL-819.

Expected movement: the fix removes the cost of re-deriving the method in a new session and the figures a single-pass reading gets wrong; the outcome is read the next time the analysis is run, against the baseline above, by whether every step has its section and the corrected tables reproduce.

Provenance: batch 261, cluster C10b (session ai-dlc-d5), operator decision of 2026-11-20 (durable form agreed); id allocated by the lead.

**PARTIAL (batch 261, cluster E8; no LANDED line).** Item 4 is built: `scripts/validate-efficiency-report-coverage.sh`, arm PE1, holds a report that declares itself under the runbook to a section per `core/skills/ai-dlc/steps/*.md` file, the list derived from the directory. On the real tree it exits 0 with 5 SKIP (the five older reports, each "legacy, predates the runbook") and 1 PASS (`pipeline-efficiency-s323-opportunities-b261.md`, 24 of 24); those SKIPs measure nothing, so they are not the false-positive set. The enumerated set, measured by copying each of the five older reports into a scratch repo under a non-legacy name, prepending the declaration token `(../plans/pipeline-efficiency-analysis.md)` within its first 5 lines and running PE1 with `AI_DLC_PROJECT_ROOT` on the scratch repo (the output names the copy paths): each of the five exits 1 with 24 findings, each "has no counted `Step files:` declaration for <step file>" (every step file plus `ai-dlc-update/SKILL.md`), and none is MALFORMED. The five: `pipeline-efficiency-s317-s318.md`, `pipeline-efficiency-s317-s322-b259.md`, `pipeline-efficiency-s317-s322.md`, `pipeline-efficiency-s323-complete-b261.md`, `pipeline-efficiency-s323-provisional-b259.md`. They fail only because they carry no `Step files:` lines; the hard-listed legacy SKIP is what keeps them green. Operator ruling, verbatim: "Skip counts as met." (operator ruling, batch 261 (AskUserQuestion; time not recorded), relayed by ai-dlc-1d). It discharges the false-positive clause: the five hard-listed pre-runbook reports, SKIPped by name, satisfy "none of them may fail". Narrowings in the check: the five older reports are hard-listed by name, the expected step list is taken as of the report's first-add commit, the second-mention rule (a declared step name counts only when it also appears on another line of the same section), and SKIP when no reports exist at all. ## BL-1207 — the readset-skip fixture's SLOT KILL arm failed once with `expected '1|2|0|0', got '0|2|0|0'` and is not reproduced

**DEFECT.** OPEN. Filed 2026-11-21 (batch 263, cluster H). Owner: `core/fixtures/readset-skip` (the SLOT KILL arm in `run.sh`, `slot-world.sh`).

Goal: the SLOT KILL arm's verdict does not depend on load or on what a previous arm left alive (BL-868). One done condition: the cause is found and a deterministic arm holds the shape.

Record: one `scripts/seed-verdict-store.sh readset-skip` run on cff73edcb's tree (before the fixture's `tp=` read moved, while the three TERM-killed seeds' descendants may still have been alive) failed `SLOT KILL: expected '1|2|0|0', got '0|2|0|0'`. Not reproduced: an instrumented plain run of the whole fixture passed (`pre=1 gate=1 hold=1 up=1 lpalive=1 galive=1`) and the next seed passed. The arm (`run.sh` kill-gate, about `:5827-5860`) reads no line that batch 263 H edited, and `core/fixtures/readset-skip/slot-world.sh:198` sources only the READSET_LOCAL span. Candidate, not confirmed: `pre` needs the last recorded group `g` to be live, and `slot-world.sh:245` records the live control's pid into the same file as the deriver's group, which is not a group leader.

Work list:

1. Find the cause: reproduce the `0` in the first field, or show from the code which recorded pid `pre` reads and when it can be dead.
2. Replace the arm's reading with one that cannot depend on timing or on a surviving process from an earlier arm, proved once by hand to fail on the seeded shape and pass without it.

**PARTIAL (batch 264, cluster D).** Item 1 advanced, not done. A red from the SLOT KILL or SLOT SHELLKILL arm now prints each of the eight parts of the `pre` chain (gate, a-hold, a-stream-up, lp-set, lp-live, g-set, g-live, world-live) as 1 (held), 0 (failed) or `-` (not reached): `slot_kill_drive` in `core/fixtures/readset-skip/run.sh` evaluates them one at a time, short-circuited as the `&&` chain was, and writes them to a file both arms' failure lines print. The verdict string and the ok lines are unchanged. Commit 7abbcceab. Still open: the cause of the one `0|2|0|0` red (item 1) and the deterministic arm (item 2).

**PARTIAL (batch 265, cluster D).** Item 1 advanced, cause not found. The red's tree (cff73edcb) runs the same world: `core/fixtures/readset-skip/slot-world.sh` is byte-identical there and on origin/main (blob 6d1f18a0d; control, `VERSION`, differs), and `slot_kill_drive` differs only by 7abbcceab's per-part breakdown. The candidate in the Record paragraph is refuted. The live control records its pid and writes `live.checked` before the world launches deriver A (`slot-world.sh:245`, `:248`), and A records itself after it (`slot-world.sh:289`), so `tail -1` of the groups file is A's group. Even a last line naming the live control would pass, because it leads its own group (`set -m`, `slot-world.sh:244-247`). Forced in a scratch copy, the control's line written last reads `1|2|0|0`, and no `set -m` reads `1|2|0|0`. Only both together read `0|2|0|0`, and the shipped code has neither. Ruled out: a stale `slot-world.*` directory (T is a fresh `mktemp -d` for each call, `core/fixtures/readset-skip/run.sh:5923`), a partly written groups line, and a lock or slot left by the TERM-killed seeds (every path deriver A uses is local to the world, so a held slot would hang the run, not turn it red). The path the code allows: deriver A dies or refuses before `a-hold` (`slot-world.sh:214`), so the world's `hold` check fails before it writes the gate. The world then kills and reaps its own recorded groups and exits. Before this release `slot_kill_drive` ignored `aw_wait`'s return of 1 (`704a4eacd:core/fixtures/readset-skip/run.sh:5926`), so the arm reads gate absent with both groups recorded and none surviving: exactly `0|2|0|0`. Once the gate is written, `pre=0` needs a process outside the code to kill the live control, A's group or the world (a delayed kill by pid landing on a reused pid); that is not audited. Why the cause cannot be named from the record: on every red the evidence was destroyed. Before this release the world's output went to `/dev/null` (`704a4eacd:core/fixtures/readset-skip/run.sh:5923`), and its EXIT trap removed `hold/aout`, which holds A's die text, with `rm -rf "$W"` (`slot-world.sh:96`). This release adds the instrument: the world's stdout and stderr go to `$T/world.out` (`core/fixtures/readset-skip/run.sh:5927`); `SW_KEEP=1` keeps the world's directory, including `hold/aout` and `hold/order`, when the world exits on its own (`slot-world.sh:96`; a SIGKILLed world never runs that path); and `aw_wait`'s return of 1 (`core/fixtures/readset-skip/run.sh:5931`) makes the verdict's first field `exited` (`core/fixtures/readset-skip/run.sh:5953`) and the arm's bad line print the world's FAIL lines, its output tail, A's aout tail and the order file (`core/fixtures/readset-skip/run.sh:5933-5937`, `:5973`, `:6020`). The next red names A's death, or else an outside kill. Still open: the cause (the next red names it), and item 2.

## BL-1212 — subagents and the stall block order whole Reads of files over 16 KB, which context-mode denies: 48 protected-path denials on graph since 0.1184

**DEFECT.** Filed 2026-11-21 (batch 264, cluster D). Owner: `core/scripts/gen-round-briefs.sh`, `core/scripts/render-agent-definitions.sh`, `core/hooks/ai-dlc-continue.sh`.

Goal: no AI/DLC instruction tells an agent to Read a file over 16 KB in one call. One done condition: every instruction behind a recorded denial is bounded, and the remaining denial class is closed upstream or by a slice.

Record: context-mode denies a whole native Read of a file over 16 KB. On graph, 48 denials of protected paths since 0.1184. The ones with an instruction behind them: 20 from the remediator brief `gen-round-briefs.sh:214` ("Read $ROLE (whole file)"); 24 from lead-written briefs to a rendered agent, which `render-agent-definitions.sh:236` told to "Read it" whole; 1 from the stall block's "Re-read the current step file" (`ai-dlc-continue.sh:2139`). The other 3 (bucket C) had no instruction behind them. The story-file lines `:196` and `:202` had no denials on record, but 340 of graph's 1,196 story files are over 16 KB (a contract figure, not re-derived). All 265 step-file denials in the record (every engine version) are over 16384 bytes, and 264 of them name `.claude/skills/ai-dlc/steps/<base>`, the path the `:2139` resolver measures. Leaving the role-file Read out was considered and rejected: dispatch-guard rewrites `subagent_type` only for a bound definition (`:704-716`), and its bounded-Read fallback (`:676`) never fires for a brief that names `team-roles/<role>.md`.

Work list:

1. Bound the four instruction sites: `:214`, `:236` (the role file only), `:196`/`:202` (one Read, or chunks when over 16 KB), and `:2139` (the clause only when the step file is over 16384 bytes, so a whole step Read still closes the handoff and recover gates). Every clause halves a chunk's limit when the chunk is refused for size.
2. Built in batch 265 (the paragraph below): `core/skills/ai-dlc/steps/gate-validation.md:313` "Read `docs/escalations/pending.md` (if it exists)" read `docs/escalations/pending.md` whole (591,630 bytes on graph). Chunks do not fit it; it needs a slice or a query of the open entries. Close receipt, to become this entry's `verify: sh` line when it closes (a PARTIAL entry carries `verify: manual`, arm R12): `grep -qF 'validate-escalation-status-vocabulary.sh --open docs/escalations/pending.md' core/skills/ai-dlc/steps/gate-validation.md || exit 1; ! grep -q 'Read .docs/escalations/pending.md. (if it exists)' core/skills/ai-dlc/steps/gate-validation.md`. It reads open (exit 1) at fd61780af. The filed first clause, `CHECK_LOADED: 2`, is a check-id anchor present at base and so vacuous; the positive grep for the new command line replaces it, and the `! grep` clause stays. The positive clause is what tells a replaced bullet from a deleted one.
3. Narrowed in batch 266 (the paragraph below): bucket C, the 3 denials with no instruction behind them. ## BL-1221 — pre-push consumer-layout selection: a skip on a confirmed placement record is named nowhere, and one box-wide record file per fixture lets pushes from different trees invalidate each other's `<fx>@consumer` units

**NOTE.** Filed 2026-11-22 (batch 264, cluster L). Owner: `.githooks/pre-push` (`cl_select`, `cl_publish`; hook copies bound by I66).

Goal: a push log names every `<fx>@consumer` unit it did not run, and a placement record written by one tree is not overwritten by another. One done condition: the log names the confirmed-record skips, and `cl_publish` keys or guards its record so a push from tree B leaves tree A's record intact.

Baseline: 24 of 38 placement records written at 10:56:02 on 2026-11-22 hold installed `run.sh` sha256 values that match no revision of `core/fixtures/<fx>/run.sh` in any ref or any of the 58 worktrees (control: `adversarial-shard-merge-c` and `-d` found at 56877eb4d); the other 14 match a historical revision. The claimed 10:49:00 rewrite did not reproduce (none at that mtime; 36 at 11:09:53). The waste per push is not yet measured; item 3 owns it.

Work list:

1. Name the confirmed-record skips. `.githooks/pre-push:3376` "counted on the selection line and not named" says an `<fx>@consumer` unit skipped on an unchanged, confirmed record is counted and not named. The named sites are `:3369` "consumer layout: %s of %s shipping fixture(s)", the `$4 == "d"` skips at `:3371`, `:3383` "skipped on a pass recorded elsewhere" (unconfirmed-record skips only) and `:3524` "PENDING count is unrecorded". A by-name coverage check over the push log cannot tell such a unit from a gap; the count is recoverable only by subtraction.
2. Key the placement records by content, or have `cl_publish` refuse to overwrite a record a different tree wrote. Records are one file per fixture, `<vs>/consumer-placement-keys/<repo root commit>/<fx>.key` (`rec_home`, `:3301`), with no per-tree or per-clone component, and `cl_publish` (`:3419` `mv "$kd/$2.key.tmp.$$" "$kd/$2.key"`) replaces the old file, so the last writer across every tree and clone on the box wins.
3. Measure `<fx>@consumer` reruns per push before and after, from `.git/ai-dlc-suite-key.log` and `.git/ai-dlc-fixture-durations`, and write the outcome beside the baseline.

**PARTIAL (v0.1233.0).** Batch 265, cluster H. Items 1 and 2 are built; item 3 is owed (the before and after `<fx>@consumer` reruns per push, read off the gate record after landing). Item 1: the selection prints a `placement records:` line naming each `<fx>@consumer` unit skipped on a confirmed record (the `.rskip` set minus `.vs.u`), naming a content-keyed (`h`) skip on its own `placement records:` line as a content-keyed pass, never as a confirmed record, because a census-written side record was never confirmed. Item 2: `cl_publish` keeps `<kd>/<fx>.key` and also writes `<kd>/<fx>.k/<sha256 of the record's non-`#` rows>`; the `cl_select` reader turns a row that is both `run` and flag `k` into `skip` with reason `h` when the prospective record's row hash has a side record, so a record written by another tree is no longer displaced. A record written before this build reads exactly as at base; `quiet()` and `.unconfirmed` stay per fixture. Both hooks carry it (I66). D3 as built: the `h` skip applies in census mode when `AI_DLC_CL_DIST_OUT` is named, so `scripts/predict-push-set.sh` predicts it as `d` is predicted, and a real census still runs every unit (arm `cl.hp`). D2 as built: an `h` skip's `#pending` count is read from its own side record (`.cl/.kpn`), not from `<fx>.key`, and `cl_publish` copies the side record from its private temporary file before the `mv` (arm `cl.h` poisons the foreign record's count). The filed receipt passed a never-overwrite wedge and a side copy nothing reads, and would now also pass this build without testing the reader; it is withdrawn, and the entry carries `verify: manual` while item 3 is open (arm R12). Intended close receipt, for item 3's landing: `for h in .githooks/pre-push core/git-hooks/pre-push; do [ -f $h ] || exit 9; grep -q 'placement records:' $h || exit 1; grep -qF '>> "$c/.hhit"' $h || exit 1; done; grep -q 'cl.h' core/fixtures/consumer-suite-pool/run.sh || exit 9` together with the outcome line beside the baseline; the reader itself is driven by arm `cl.h` of `core/fixtures/consumer-suite-pool/run.sh`.

## BL-1255 — the ledger-reverify fixture's shards are unbalanced, and no per-unit cost is read to choose a move

**NOTE (efficiency).** OPEN. Filed 2026-11-26, batch 268, cluster M, re-homed from BL-583; id allocated by lead ai-dlc-72. Owner: `core/fixtures/ledger-reverify*`.

The cost lands in two places: this repo's pre-push gate, and every consumer push that dispatches shard a. Shard a (`ledger-reverify`) ships, and graph's pushes run it. Shards b and c are `.dist-only` and run only here.

Goal: the three `ledger-reverify` shards are balanced by a move chosen from recorded per-unit costs, or the record shows that no move gains.

- The loaded-cost record read shard a 555 s, b 108 s and c 60 s (BL-583's v0.1146.0 PARTIAL, from `.git/ai-dlc-fixture-durations` in the main checkout).
- The suite is width-bound: wall clock is summed unit cost / width, at least the longest unit. A full suite then summed 15176 s of plain rows, about 1265 s at width 12.
- In the 45 push logs of the batch-257 session scratchpads, priced at the same record, shard a was dispatched in 3 and was the floor in 2: 39 units at 488 s per 12 workers, and 26 units at 334 s.
- Blocked two ways. A unit moved out of a can go to b or c, but those are `.dist-only`, so a consumer would stop running it. The other option is a new shipping shard (`uninstall.sh` plus both manifest copies). And no per-unit seconds are recorded to choose a move.

"A step with no measured value goes" (`.claude/rules/operator-rulings.md`) applies to any unit the reading shows to be a repeat.

Baseline: s324 (open; graph's first `(s324)` commit is b00756c1e, 2026-11-21T01:57Z). 1 of the 26 recovered graph push outputs from that time on dispatched shard a: graph session 40bd16ae, an `/ai-dlc-update` pull, at 2026-11-26T02:23Z, file `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-n8-git-graph/40bd16ae-64db-4558-ab98-f70ce5909f9a/scratchpad/push.txt`. It printed `done 7/56  ok ledger-reverify`, `read-set keys: 56 of 194`, and a fixture-suite `step elapsed 344s`. The output prints no per-unit seconds. In the consumer layout the unit is plain `ledger-reverify`, with no `@consumer` suffix. By session: 0 of 15 outputs from `/ai-dlc` sessions, 1 of 10 from `/ai-dlc-update` sessions, and 0 of 1 unclassified (5ccc89cc). These are the recovered outputs, the paths listed in `blobs.json` of the batch-268 m1167 scratchpad, each read directly. They are not every push: many push calls left no recoverable output. Counting command: over those files with a time at or after 2026-11-21T01:57Z, `/usr/bin/grep -lE 'done +[0-9]+/[0-9]+ +[^ ]+ +ledger-reverify$'`. Control in the same invocation: the kept sibling `ledger-reverify-unfalsifiable` reads 4 files. Distribution side: shard a 555 s, b 108 s and c 60 s, loaded costs from `.git/ai-dlc-fixture-durations` as read for BL-583's v0.1146.0 PARTIAL; shard a was the floor in 2 of 45 push logs.

Expected movement: after a move, the gap between shard a's loaded cost and b's and c's narrows. A graph push that dispatches shard a then spends less of its fixture-suite step waiting on it. If item 1's reading shows no move gains, nothing moves and the entry records that.

Work list:
